## Athletics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Athletics")]

Main article: [UC Irvine Anteaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters "UC Irvine Anteaters")

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_logo.svg/120px-UC_Irvine_Anteaters_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UC_Irvine_Anteaters_logo.svg)

UC Irvine Anteaters logo

UC Irvine's sports teams are known as the [Anteaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anteaters "Anteaters") and the student body is known as Antourage. They currently participate in the [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association")'s Division I, as members of the [Big West Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_West_Conference "Big West Conference")[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-152) and the [Mountain Pacific Sports Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_Pacific_Sports_Federation "Mountain Pacific Sports Federation").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-153) In the early years of the school's existence, the teams participated at the NCAA Division II level with great success as explained in the UC Irvine Anteaters page. UC Irvine fields nationally competitive teams in baseball, basketball, cross country, golf, soccer, track and field, volleyball and water polo. The university has won 28 national championships in nine different sports, and fielded 64 individual national champions, 53 Olympians and over 500 All-Americans.

The university's most recent NCAA Division I national championship was won by [the men's volleyball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_men's_volleyball "UC Irvine Anteaters men's volleyball") in 2013. UC Irvine men's volleyball won four national championships in 2007, 2009, 2012 and 2013.

UC Irvine won three NCAA Division I men's water polo titles, with championships in 1970, 1982 and 1989.

[UC Irvine Anteaters baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_baseball "UC Irvine Anteaters baseball") won back-to-back national championships at the NCAA College Division College World Series and the NCAA Division II College World Series in 1973 and 1974. Anteater baseball moved to the NCAA Division I level. The 2007 baseball team finished 3rd at the College World Series, and in 2009 the baseball team earned a No. 1 national ranking in NCAA Division I polls from Baseball America and Collegiate Baseball for the first time, as well as a national seed and the right to host an NCAA Regional. The 2014 baseball team returned to the College World Series and finished 5th.

UCI Anteater's golf team won the NCAA Division II national team championship in 1975 with team member Jerry Wisz winning the individual title. At the NCAA national championships in 1973, 1974 and 1976, those teams finished second twice and fourth the other year. These teams included seven All-Americans.

[In 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), for the first time, the [UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_men's_basketball "UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball") team appeared in the [Division I tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship"). It was narrowly defeated in a first-round tournament game by [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals_men's_basketball "Louisville Cardinals men's basketball"). The Anteaters made their second NCAA appearance [in 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), beating fourth-seed [Kansas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_University "Kansas State University") for their first March Madness win ever.

## People

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: People")]

Main article: [List of University of California, Irvine people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_University_of_California,_Irvine_people "List of University of California, Irvine people")

UC Irvine has more than 265,000 living alumni.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-154) These include astronauts ([Tracy Caldwell Dyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Caldwell_Dyson "Tracy Caldwell Dyson")), athletes ([Steve Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Scott_(athlete) "Steve Scott (athlete)"), [Scott Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Brooks "Scott Brooks"), [Greg Louganis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Louganis "Greg Louganis") and 53 Olympians), Broadway, film, and television actors ([Bob Gunton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Gunton "Bob Gunton"), [James LeGros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_LeGros "James LeGros"), [Jon Lovitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Lovitz "Jon Lovitz"), [Brian Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Thompson_(actor) "Brian Thompson (actor)"), [Teal Wicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teal_Wicks "Teal Wicks"), [Windell Middlebrooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windell_Middlebrooks "Windell Middlebrooks")), technological innovators ([Roy Fielding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Fielding "Roy Fielding"), [Paul Mockapetris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mockapetris "Paul Mockapetris"), and [Patrick J. Hanratty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_J._Hanratty "Patrick J. Hanratty")), educators ([Erin Gruwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_Gruwell "Erin Gruwell")), musicians ([Kevin Kwan Loucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Kwan_Loucks "Kevin Kwan Loucks")), and scientists ([Mika Tosca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mika_Tosca "Mika Tosca")).[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-UC-155)

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/UC_Irvine_Reines_Hall.jpg/250px-UC_Irvine_Reines_Hall.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UC_Irvine_Reines_Hall.jpg)

[Frederick Reines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Reines "Frederick Reines") Hall in the School of Physical Sciences, named after one of the UCI faculty members to receive the [Nobel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize").

Five people affiliated with UCI have been honored with the [Nobel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize"): three faculty members, one postdoctoral scholar, and one alumnus. In 1995, professor [Frank Sherwood Rowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sherwood_Rowland "Frank Sherwood Rowland") along with postdoctoral student [Mario Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Molina "Mario Molina") won the [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") while [Frederick Reines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Reines "Frederick Reines") won the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"). In 1974, Rowland and Molina worked together to discover the harmful effects of [CFCs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorofluorocarbon "Chlorofluorocarbon") on the [ozone layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozone_layer "Ozone layer"), while Reines received the Nobel Prize for his work in discovering the [neutrino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutrino "Neutrino"). In 2004, [Irwin Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irwin_Rose "Irwin Rose"), a professor at the School of Medicine, was co-awarded the [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") along with two professors from the [Technion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technion "Technion") for the discovery of ubiquitin-mediated [protein degradation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteolysis "Proteolysis"). Additionally, [David MacMillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_MacMillan "David MacMillan"), who completed his PhD. from UCI in 1996 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2021 for the development of asymmetric [organocatalysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organocatalysis "Organocatalysis").[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-156)

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Rowland_Hall_2025.jpg/250px-Rowland_Hall_2025.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rowland_Hall_2025.jpg)

Rowland Hall, named after [Frank "Sherry" Rowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Sherwood_Rowland "F. Sherwood Rowland"), who won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery that [CFCs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorofluorocarbon "Chlorofluorocarbon") contribute to [ozone depletion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozone_depletion "Ozone depletion"). It is a [National Historic Chemical Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Chemical_Landmarks "National Historic Chemical Landmarks").[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-157)

Seven [Pulitzer Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize "Pulitzer Prize") winners have been associated with UCI, including three faculty members and four alumni.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Notable_Alumni-17)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Faculty_Awards_and_Honors-158) These include [Michael Chabon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Chabon "Michael Chabon"), who won the [Pulitzer Prize for Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Fiction "Pulitzer Prize for Fiction") in 2001 for _[The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Amazing\_Adventures\_of\_Kavalier\_&\_Clay "The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay")_, and [Richard Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ford "Richard Ford"), who won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1996 for _[Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence\_Day\_(Ford\_novel) "Independence Day (Ford novel)")_. Claude Yarbrough (aka [Jonathan Pendragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Pendragon "Jonathan Pendragon")), class of '76, is one of the most influential magicians of the 20th and 21st centuries.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-159)[Thomas Keneally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Keneally "Thomas Keneally") was a visiting professor at UCI in 1985 (when he taught the graduate fiction workshop) and again from 1991 to 1995 (when he was a visiting professor in the writing program).[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-160) Keneally is most famous for his book _[Schindler's Ark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schindler's\_Ark "Schindler's Ark")_ (1982) (later republished as _Schindler's List_), which won the Booker Prize and is the basis of the film _[Schindler's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schindler's\_List "Schindler's List")_ that was directed by [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg").

The Comparative Literature and Philosophy departments at Irvine have accommodated distinguished intellectuals of international acclaim, including [Jacques Derrida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Derrida "Jacques Derrida"), a philosopher and critic most commonly associated with postmodern and post-structuralist thought, who held a position at the University of California, Irvine Department of Comparative Literature from 1986 to his death in 2004; his colleague, [Jean-François Lyotard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Fran%C3%A7ois_Lyotard "Jean-François Lyotard"), who taught at UCI from 1987 until 1994;[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-161) Fellow at the [American Academy of Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Academy_of_Arts_and_Sciences "American Academy of Arts and Sciences"), British philosopher [Margaret Gilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Gilbert "Margaret Gilbert") best known for her founding contributions to the analytic philosophy of social phenomena; and British philosopher and [FRSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FRSE "FRSE")[Duncan Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duncan_Pritchard "Duncan Pritchard").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-162)

In addition to the Department of Philosophy at UCI, its sister department, the Department of Logic and Philosophy of Science, which together are ranked as one of the top philosophy programs in the world,[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-www.humanities.uci.edu-163) also accommodates philosophers such as [Brian Skyrms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Skyrms "Brian Skyrms"), known for his contributions on [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory "Game theory") and [social norms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_norms "Social norms"); [Jeffrey A. Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_A._Barrett "Jeffrey A. Barrett"), known for his contributions to [philosophy of physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_physics "Philosophy of physics"); and [Kai Wehmeier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kai_Wehmeier "Kai Wehmeier"), known for his contributions to [Frege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frege "Frege").

[Ralph J. Cicerone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_J._Cicerone "Ralph J. Cicerone"), an earth system science professor and former chancellor of UCI, served as president of the [National Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Academy_of_Sciences "United States National Academy of Sciences") from 2005 to 2016.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-164)

Three UCI faculty members have been named [National Medal of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Science "National Medal of Science") recipients.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-faculty-165) In January 2009, UCI Professor Reg Penner won the [Faraday Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faraday_Medal "Faraday Medal") for his research with [nanowires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanowire "Nanowire").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-166)

The **University of California, Irvine** (**UCI** or **UC Irvine**) is a [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university "Public university")[land-grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land-grant_university "Land-grant university")[research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in [Irvine, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_California "Irvine, California"), United States. One of the ten campuses of the [University of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California "University of California") system, UCI offers 87 undergraduate degrees and 129 graduate and professional degrees, and roughly 30,000 undergraduates and 7,000 graduate students were enrolled at UCI as of Fall 2024.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Enrollment_Data-7) The university is [classified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Classification_of_Institutions_of_Higher_Education "Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education") among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity" and had $609.6 million in [research and development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_and_development "Research and development") expenditures in 2023, ranking it 56th nationally.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-research_expend-12) UCI became a member of the [Association of American Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities "Association of American Universities") in 1996.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-13)

The university administers the [UC Irvine Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Medical_Center "UC Irvine Medical Center"), a large [teaching hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teaching_hospital "Teaching hospital") in [Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange,_California "Orange, California"), and [its affiliated health sciences system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Health_Sciences "UC Irvine Health Sciences"); the [University of California, Irvine, Arboretum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine,_Arboretum "University of California, Irvine, Arboretum"); and a portion of the [University of California Natural Reserve System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California_Natural_Reserve_System "University of California Natural Reserve System"). UC Irvine set up the first Earth System Science Department in the United States.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Obama-15)

The [UC Irvine Anteaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters "UC Irvine Anteaters") currently compete in the [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Division_I_(NCAA) "Division I (NCAA)") as members of the [Big West Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_West_Conference "Big West Conference").[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-16)

As of 2026, alumni, academics, and affiliates of UCI include 5 [Nobel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") laureates, 7 [Pulitzer Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize "Pulitzer Prize") winners, and a [Dan David Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_David_Prize "Dan David Prize") winner.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Notable_Alumni-17)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]

The University of California, Irvine (with [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_San_Diego "University of California, San Diego") and [Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Santa_Cruz "University of California, Santa Cruz")) was one of three new University of California campuses established in the 1960s under the [California Master Plan for Higher Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Master_Plan_for_Higher_Education "California Master Plan for Higher Education").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-18) During the 1950s, the [University of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California "University of California") saw the need for the new campuses to handle the expected increase in enrollment from the [post-war baby boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-World_War_II_baby_boom "Post-World War II baby boom"). One of the new campuses was to be in the Los Angeles area; the location selected was Irvine Ranch, an area of agricultural land bisecting [Orange County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_County,_California "Orange County, California") from north to south. This site was chosen to accommodate the county's growing population, complement the growth of nearby [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA") and [UC Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Riverside "UC Riverside"), and allow for the construction of a master planned community in the surrounding area.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-site_selection-19)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/UCISign.jpg/250px-UCISign.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCISign.jpg)

One of two identical UCI signs that face the main campus' western entrance

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/LyndonBJohnsonUCIrvineGroundbreaking1964.jpg/250px-LyndonBJohnsonUCIrvineGroundbreaking1964.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LyndonBJohnsonUCIrvineGroundbreaking1964.jpg)

President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") at the university's groundbreaking ceremony in June 1964

On June 20, 1964, U.S. President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") dedicated UC Irvine before a crowd of 15,000 people, and on October 4, 1965, the campus began operations with 1,589 students, 241 staff members, 119 faculty, and 43 teaching assistants.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-21) However, many of UCI's buildings were still under construction, and landscaping was still in progress, with the campus only at 75% completion.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-lib-22) By June 25, 1966, UCI held its first Commencement with fourteen students, which conferred ten Bachelor of Arts degrees, three Master of Arts degrees, and one Doctor of Philosophy degree.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-23)

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Development")]

Unlike most other University of California campuses, UCI was not named for the city it was built in; at the time of the university's founding (1965), the current city of [Irvine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_CA "Irvine, CA") (incorporated in 1971) did not exist. The name "Irvine" is a reference to [James Irvine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Irvine_(landowner) "James Irvine (landowner)"), a landowner who administered the 94,000-acre (38,000 ha) Irvine Ranch. In 1960, [The Irvine Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Irvine_Company "The Irvine Company") sold 1,000 acres (400 ha) of the Irvine Ranch to the University of California for one dollar, since company policy prohibited the donation of property to a public entity.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-site_selection-19) On campus, UC Irvine's first Chancellor, [Daniel G. Aldrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_G._Aldrich "Daniel G. Aldrich") selected a wide variety of [Mediterranean-climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") flora and fauna, feeling that it served an "aesthetic, environmental, and educational [purpose]."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-24) To plan the remainder of the ranch, the university hired [William Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Pereira "William Pereira") and Associates. Pereira intended for the UC Irvine campus to complement the neighboring community, and it became clear that the original 1,000-acre (400 ha) grant would not suffice. In 1964, the university purchased an additional 510 acres (210 ha) in 1964 for housing and commercial developments.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-site_selection-19)

Much of the land that was not purchased by UCI (which is now occupied by the cities of Irvine, [Tustin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tustin,_California "Tustin, California"), and [Newport Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Beach,_California "Newport Beach, California")) remains held by [The Irvine Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Irvine_Company "The Irvine Company"), but the completion of the university rapidly drove the development of Orange County. The City of Irvine became incorporated and established in 1971 and 1975, respectively.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-site_selection-19) UCI remains the second-largest employer in [Orange County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_County,_California "Orange County, California"), employing 34,076 people as of Fall 2024 and generating an estimated $8 billion in annual economic impact in California.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-26)

Aldrich developed the campus's first academic plan around a College of Letters and Science, a Graduate School of Administration, and a School of Engineering.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Stadtman_Page_419-27) The "principal author" of the plan was [Ivan Hinderaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Hinderaker "Ivan Hinderaker"), who served under Aldrich as UCI's vice-chancellor for academic affairs before departing to become the second chancellor of UC Riverside.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Stadtman_Page_419-27) The UCI College of Letters and Science was to be divided into five divisions which together would initially offer about a dozen majors: Biological Sciences, Fine Arts, Humanities, Physical Sciences, and Social Sciences.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Stadtman_Page_419-27) Hinderaker came up with the idea "to appoint deans with strong authority for each of the divisions and to give them as much freedom as possible in determining the internal organization of their divisions".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Stadtman_Page_419-27) In 1967, the UCI Academic Senate voted to redesignate the divisions as "schools", with all their deans reporting directly to the vice chancellor for academic affairs.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-Stadtman_Page_419-27) This is why schools became the dominant academic unit at UCI, in contrast to the relatively large colleges at the older UC campuses.

In 1967, the California College of Medicine (originally a [school of osteopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteopathic_medicine_in_the_United_States "Osteopathic medicine in the United States") founded in 1896 and the oldest continuously operating medical college in the [Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States "Southwestern United States")) became part of UC Irvine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-som.uci.edu-29) In 1976, plans to establish an on-campus hospital were set aside, with the university instead purchasing the Orange County Medical Center (renamed the [UC Irvine Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Medical_Center "UC Irvine Medical Center")) around 12 miles from UC Irvine, in the City of Orange.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-som.uci.edu-29)

### Recent history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Recent history")]

On November 30, 2007, the [Office of Civil Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Civil_Rights "Office of Civil Rights") of the [United States Department of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education") issued a report finding insufficient evidence in support of allegations that Jewish students at UCI were harassed and subjected to a hostile environment based on their religious beliefs. The agency ultimately found that none of the incidents leading to the allegations qualified as "sufficiently severe, pervasive or persistent as to interfere with or limit the ability of an individual to participate in from the services, activities or privileges" provided by UCI, and that university officials had acted appropriately in response to each incident. In December 2007, UCI Administration was cleared of anti-semitism complaints by the [US Department of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education")'s [Office for Civil Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_for_Civil_Rights "Office for Civil Rights").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-OCR-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-31) Following a speech by Chancellor Drake at the national [Hillel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillel_International "Hillel International") meeting in Washington, D.C. in March 2008, Anteaters for Israel, along with three other Jewish organizations, issued a press release defending Drake and claiming that the anti-Semitic activity was "exaggerated".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-32)

#### Irvine 11 controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Irvine 11 controversy")]

Main article: [Irvine 11 controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine_11_controversy "Irvine 11 controversy")

In 2010, eleven students from the [Muslim Student Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Student_Union_of_the_University_of_California,_Irvine "Muslim Student Union of the University of California, Irvine") disrupted a speech by Israeli Ambassador [Michael Oren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Oren "Michael Oren"). The students and the student's union involved were first disciplined by UCI and then had criminal charges brought against them. They were convicted of misdemeanor charges and sentenced to three years probation, community service, and fines. This led to a debate on whether the students' protest was free speech and whether filing criminal charges against them was fair after UCI had already disciplined them.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-34) Critics argued that the students were victims of [selective prosecution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_prosecution "Selective prosecution") and that they were targeted because they were Muslims and supported the [Palestinians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict "Israeli–Palestinian conflict").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-38)

In early July 2018, UC Irvine removed benefactor [Francisco J. Ayala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_J._Ayala "Francisco J. Ayala")'s name from its biology school and central science library after an internal investigation by the university's Office of Equal Opportunity and Diversity substantiated a number of sexual harassment claims. Chancellor Gillman also authorized the removal of the Ayala name from graduate fellowships, scholar programs, and endowed chairs. Ayala resigned July 1, 2018 and was ordered to abstain from future university activities, following the university's consultative procedures that include a faculty review committee. The results from the investigation were compiled in a 97-page report, which included testimony from victims of Ayala.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-41)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-43)

## Campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Campus")]

Main article: [Campus of the University of California, Irvine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campus_of_the_University_of_California,_Irvine "Campus of the University of California, Irvine")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Campus_of_the_University_of_California%2C_Irvine_%28aerial_view%2C_circa_2006%29.jpg/250px-Campus_of_the_University_of_California%2C_Irvine_%28aerial_view%2C_circa_2006%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Campus_of_the_University_of_California,_Irvine_(aerial_view,_circa_2006).jpg)

UCI's core campus and surrounding areas in 2006. Aldrich Park is in the center.

The layout of the core campus resembles a rough circle with its center being Aldrich Park (initially known as Campus Park), lined up by the Ring Mall and buildings surrounding the road. Academic units are positioned relative to the center, wherein undergraduate schools are closer to the center than the graduate schools.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-44)

Aldrich Park forms part of a campus-wide urban forest of approximately 30,000 trees.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-45)

Two ceremonial trees were planted in 1990, one for Arbor Day and the second for former chancellor Daniel Aldrich who had died that year. On the first anniversary of the September 11th tragedies, the chancellor planted a bay laurel tree in remembrance of the heroes and victims of the events of September 11, 2001. The tree itself was a gift from the UCI Staff Assembly. Reforestation and landscape revitalization efforts have shifted plantings away from earlier stands of fast-growing eucalyptus toward more native and ecologically suitable California species.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-47) The park is also reported to contain approximately 51 varieties of trees and is regarded as the first park in the City of Irvine.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-48)

### Surroundings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Surroundings")]

See also: [UCI Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCI_Medical_Center "UCI Medical Center"); [University of California, Irvine, Arboretum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine,_Arboretum "University of California, Irvine, Arboretum"); and [University of California Natural Reserve System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California_Natural_Reserve_System "University of California Natural Reserve System")

While the university is located in Irvine, the campus is directly bounded by the city of [Newport Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Beach "Newport Beach") and the community of [Newport Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Coast "Newport Coast"). The western side of the campus borders the [San Diego Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Creek "San Diego Creek") and the San Joaquin Freshwater Marsh Reserve, through which Campus Drive connects UCI to the [405 freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_405_(California) "Interstate 405 (California)"). The northern and eastern sides of UCI are adjacent to Irvine proper; the eastern side of the campus is delineated by Bonita Canyon Road, which turns into [Culver Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culver_Drive,_Irvine,_California "Culver Drive, Irvine, California") at its northern terminus. [California State Route 73](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_Route_73 "California State Route 73") marks UCI's southern boundary and separates the campus from Newport Beach.

The "North Campus" houses the Facilities Management Department, the Faculty Research Facility, Central Receiving, Fleet Services, the Air Pollution Health Effects Laboratory, and the 1.2 million square foot Irvine Campus Medical Complex (ICMC). It is located next to the [UCI Arboretum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine,_Arboretum "University of California, Irvine, Arboretum"), a 12.5 acre botanic garden and research facility which maintains major plant collections from the [California Floristic Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_floristic_province "California floristic province") and [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-:2-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-50) The Arboretum is closed until further notice due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") with plans to relocate to the main campus.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-51)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-:2-49) Both the North Campus and the arboretum are located about 1 mile (2 km) from the main campus. The UCI Ecological Preserve, located on the southern edge of the main campus, comprises approximately 60 acres of [coastal sage scrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_sage_scrub "Coastal sage scrub") and [grassland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grassland "Grassland") habitat. It is managed as part of the Nature Reserve of Orange County and is used for field instruction and ecological research.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-52) In 2024, construction of the Joe C. Wen & Family UCI Health Center for Advanced Care and the Chao Family Comprehensive Cancer Center was completed. In late 2025, an all-electric 144-bed acute care hospital will follow suit, making this the nation’s first medical center to be powered by an all-electric central utilities plant.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-53)

### Libraries and study centers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Libraries and study centers")]

Main article: [University of California Libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California_Libraries "University of California Libraries")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/UCILibrary.jpg/250px-UCILibrary.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCILibrary.jpg)

Langson Library, one of the five central libraries maintained by UCI, is the main repository for most of the university's research materials and hosts many study areas.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-54)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/UC_Irvine%2C_Science_Library.JPG/250px-UC_Irvine%2C_Science_Library.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UC_Irvine,_Science_Library.JPG)

Science Library, another of the five central libraries maintained by UCI, is one of the largest consolidated science and medical libraries in the nation.

Jack Langson Library Resources for the Arts, Humanities, Education, Social Sciences, Social Ecology, and Business & Management disciplines[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-55)
Science Library One of the largest consolidated science and medical libraries in the nation. Resources for the schools of Biological Sciences, Engineering, Information and Computer Science, Physical Sciences, portions of Social Ecology, and the College of Medicine[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-56)
Grunigen Medical Library Located at [UCI Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCI_Medical_Center "UCI Medical Center"), contains 43,000 volumes of material[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-medlib-57)
Law Library Located on the bottom two floors of the Law Building[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In addition to holding a noted [critical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_theory "Critical theory") archive and Southeast Asian archive, the Libraries also contain extensive collections in Dance and Performing Arts, Regional History, and more. Additionally, Langson Library hosts an extensive East Asian collection with materials in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

Nearly all departments and schools on campus complement the resources of the UC Irvine Libraries by maintaining their own reading rooms and scholarly meeting rooms. They contain small reference collections and are the choice for more intimate lectures, graduate seminars, and study sessions. There is also the large Gateway Study Center located across from Langson Library, one of the university's original buildings and under the custody of UC Irvine Libraries. Having served formerly as a cafeteria and student center, it is now a dual-use computer lab and study area which is open nearly 24 hours.

The UCI Student Center offers a large number of study areas, auditoriums, and two food courts, and therefore is one of the most popular places to study on campus. UC Irvine also has a number of computer labs that serve as study centers. The School of Humanities maintains the Humanities Instructional Resource Center, a drop-in computer lab specializing in language and digital media. Additionally, UCI maintains five other drop-in labs, four instructional computer labs, and a number of reservation-only SmartClassrooms, some of which are open 24 hours. Other popular study areas include Aldrich Park, the Cross-Cultural Center, the Locus (a study room and computer lab used by the Campuswide Honors Program), and plazas located in every school.

### Tunnels

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Tunnels")]

A network of [tunnels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel "Tunnel") runs between many of the major buildings on campus and the Central Plant, with the major trunk passage located beneath Ring Mall. Smaller tunnels branch off from this main passage to reach individual buildings, carrying electrical and air-conditioning utilities from the Central Plant. These tunnels have been the subject of much campus lore, the most popular story being that the tunnels were constructed to facilitate the safe evacuation of faculty in the event of a student riot. The main tunnel actually contains an above-ground section, in the form of the interior of an unusually thick pedestrian bridge near the Engineering Tower, in an area where the Ring Mall crosses between two hills. The tunnels are only accessible to maintenance staff, although there are also publicly accessible tunnels which intersect the utility tunnels, such as the one that goes between the main Information & Computer Science building and the Engineering Tower.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Governance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Governance")]

Like other [University of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California "University of California") campuses, UC Irvine operates under a system of shared governance, or a partnership between the Chancellor and his administration and the faculty through the Academic Senate. The Chancellor is the chief campus officer and has authority over the campus budget.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-58) The Academic Senate has authority to determine the conditions for admission and supervise courses and curricula.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-59) The Chancellor is nominated by and is responsible to the [Regents of the University of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regents_of_the_University_of_California "Regents of the University of California") and the UC President.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-60)

After the Chancellor, the second most senior official is the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-61) the university's chief academic and operating officer. Every school on campus reports to the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost through a Dean, and all other academic and administrative units report to this office through a Vice Chancellor or chief administrator. A partial list of these units includes Campus Recreation, Intercollegiate Athletics, Planning and Budget, Student Affairs, UC Irvine Libraries, UC Irvine Medical Center, and University Advancement.

UC Irvine is categorized by _[U.S. News & World Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S.\_News\_&\_World\_Report "U.S. News & World Report")_ as "most selective" for college admissions in the United States.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-113) It was the third-most selective [University of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California "University of California") campus for the freshman class entering in the fall of 2019, as measured by the ratio of admitted students to applicants (behind [UC Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Berkeley "UC Berkeley") and [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA")).[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-114) UC Irvine received 124,231 applications for admission to the fall 2025 incoming freshman class and 35,964 were admitted, making UC Irvine's acceptance rate 28.94% for fall 2025. The first-year median weighted GPA was 4.19 for fall 2025.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-115)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-116)

The incoming 2025 freshmen were predominantly from [Orange County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_County,_California "Orange County, California") (25.7%), followed by [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County "Los Angeles County") (25.3%), [San Diego County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_County "San Diego County") (7.3%), [Riverside County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_County "Riverside County") (7.0%), and [San Bernardino County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Bernardino_County "San Bernardino County") (5.4%). Of the 2025 freshmen international students, a majority came from Asia. 67.0% were from [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), 6.1% from [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), 5.6% from [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"), 4.0% from [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan"), and a distant 1.9% from [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-117)

Admission and yield rates also vary by the residency of applicants. For Fall 2025, California residents had a selectivity rate of 21.9% out of 86,230 applicants, with a yield rate of 25.7%. Out of state residents saw greater rate of admission, with 47.5% of 16,381 applicants receiving acceptance. However, only 5.8% of those admitted went on to enroll. Of the 21,620 international students who applied, 42.8% were accepted and 11.9% went on to enroll.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-118)

That year, the most popular major for freshmen (excluding transfers) was Undeclared (15.4%), followed by Biological Sciences (12.8%), Business Administration (4.0%), Computer Science (3.9%), Public Health Sciences (3.7%), and Political Science (3.3%).

The choice to offer admission is based on the University of California's comprehensive review program, which considers a candidate's personal situation, community involvement, extracurricular activities, and academic potential in addition to the traditional high school academic record, personal statement, and entrance examination scores.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-119) While residency is not a factor in admission, it is a factor in tuition expenses, with out-of-state residents fees much greater than California residents. Since the approval of [Proposition 209](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_California_Proposition_209 "1996 California Proposition 209") in November 1996, California state law has prohibited all public universities (including UC Irvine) from practicing [affirmative action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affirmative_action "Affirmative action") as part of their admissions processes.

### Middle Earth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Middle Earth")]

Middle Earth is a [student housing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_housing "Student housing") complex that includes housing approximately 1,784 first-year students in 24 "classics" residence halls, and another 640 in two five-level "towers", a student center (Pippin Center), dining facility (Brandywine) and several resource centers.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-138) Each hall houses 48–96 students, although Quenya was built with sixty single-suite rooms originally intended for graduate students.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-139) The names of the halls and other facilities were selected from [J.R.R. Tolkien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J.R.R._Tolkien "J.R.R. Tolkien")'s [legendarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tolkien's_legendarium "Tolkien's legendarium").[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-140)

Middle Earth is located along Ring Road, toward the core of [the university's campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine_campus "University of California, Irvine campus"). The residence halls were built in three consecutive phases, beginning in 1974.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-spangenberg-141)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-142) The first phase was designed by [William Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Pereira "William Pereira").[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-143) The first phase included seven halls: Hobbiton, Isengard, Lorien, Mirkwood, Misty Mountain, Rivendell, and the Shire, along with a separate Head Resident's manufactured home called "Bag End". The second phase was built in 1989 with thirteen more halls: Balin, Harrowdale, Whispering Wood, Woodhall, Calmindon, Grey Havens, Aldor, Rohan, Gondolin, Snowbourn, Elrond, Shadowfax, and Quenya. The third phase was built in 2000 with four halls: Crickhollow, Evenstar, Oakenshield, and Valimar. The last phase was completed in the summer of 2019 and officially opened September 16, 2019; although reported in the media as being called [the two towers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Two_Towers "The Two Towers") of Middle Earth,[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-144) its two buildings are actually named Telperion and Laurelin, after the [Two Trees of Valinor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_Trees_of_Valinor "Two Trees of Valinor"). These towers house around 640 undergraduate students.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Mesa Court")]

Mesa Court is another housing community intended for freshman as part of the "First Year Experience". It houses around 3,484 students in 29 "classics" halls and four residential towers. The towers themselves accommodate 1,440 students and include study areas, computer labs, a fitness center, with shared kitchenettes and laundry facilities. Situated below "Caballo", one of the towers, is the other major dining facility on campus (The Anteatery) which can serve 780 students at maximum. Full-time graduate students are guaranteed on-campus housing for the duration of a determined "normal time to degree" for their program, and as long as they maintain good academic standing. #### Verano Place

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_California,_Irvine&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Verano Place")]

The Verano Place apartments first began housing graduate students in 1966, not long after the founding of the university.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-149) Subsequent development has supplemented the original residence halls with higher-density housing for a predominantly medical, law, and graduate student population of about 2,095.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-150)

In summer of 2022, the Verano 8 Graduate Student Housing Community was completed, adding 1,055 beds across five seven-story buildings to help alleviate the demand of a growing graduate population. Included in the housing community is a community center and an 853-stall parking garage.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-151)

## Athletics

Main article: [UC Irvine Anteaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters "UC Irvine Anteaters")

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_logo.svg/120px-UC_Irvine_Anteaters_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UC_Irvine_Anteaters_logo.svg)

UC Irvine Anteaters logo

UC Irvine's sports teams are known as the [Anteaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anteaters "Anteaters") and the student body is known as Antourage. They currently participate in the [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association")'s Division I, as members of the [Big West Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_West_Conference "Big West Conference")[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-152) and the [Mountain Pacific Sports Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_Pacific_Sports_Federation "Mountain Pacific Sports Federation").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Irvine#cite_note-153) In the early years of the school's existence, the teams participated at the NCAA Division II level with great success as explained in the UC Irvine Anteaters page. UC Irvine fields nationally competitive teams in baseball, basketball, cross country, golf, soccer, track and field, volleyball and water polo. The university has won 28 national championships in nine different sports, and fielded 64 individual national champions, 53 Olympians and over 500 All-Americans.

The university's most recent NCAA Division I national championship was won by [the men's volleyball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_men's_volleyball "UC Irvine Anteaters men's volleyball") in 2013. UC Irvine men's volleyball won four national championships in 2007, 2009, 2012 and 2013.

UC Irvine won three NCAA Division I men's water polo titles, with championships in 1970, 1982 and 1989.

[UC Irvine Anteaters baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_baseball "UC Irvine Anteaters baseball") won back-to-back national championships at the NCAA College Division College World Series and the NCAA Division II College World Series in 1973 and 1974. Anteater baseball moved to the NCAA Division I level. The 2007 baseball team finished 3rd at the College World Series, and in 2009 the baseball team earned a No. 1 national ranking in NCAA Division I polls from Baseball America and Collegiate Baseball for the first time, as well as a national seed and the right to host an NCAA Regional. The 2014 baseball team returned to the College World Series and finished 5th.

UCI Anteater's golf team won the NCAA Division II national team championship in 1975 with team member Jerry Wisz winning the individual title. At the NCAA national championships in 1973, 1974 and 1976, those teams finished second twice and fourth the other year. These teams included seven All-Americans.

[In 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), for the first time, the [UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Irvine_Anteaters_men's_basketball "UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball") team appeared in the [Division I tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship"). It was narrowly defeated in a first-round tournament game by [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals_men's_basketball "Louisville Cardinals men's basketball"). The Anteaters made their second NCAA appearance [in 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), beating fourth-seed [Kansas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_University "Kansas State University") for their first March Madness win ever.

**Michael Morhaime** (born November 3, 1967) is an American [video game developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_developer "Video game developer") and entrepreneur. He is the chief executive officer (CEO) and founder of [Dreamhaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamhaven "Dreamhaven"), located in [Irvine, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_California "Irvine, California"). Morhaime is best known as the co-founder and the former [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_(corporate_title) "President (corporate title)") of [Blizzard Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blizzard_Entertainment "Blizzard Entertainment"), a subsidiary of [Activision Blizzard, Inc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activision_Blizzard "Activision Blizzard")., that was founded in 1991 as Silicon & Synapse. He served on the Vivendi Games executive committee from January 1999, when Blizzard Entertainment, Inc. became a subsidiary of Vivendi Games, until July 2008.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Morhaime was born into a [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") family and graduated from Granada Hills High School in 1985. He is also an alumnus of [Triangle Fraternity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle_Fraternity "Triangle Fraternity")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-3) and received his [bachelor's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor's_degree "Bachelor's degree") in Electrical Engineering in 1990 from the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles") (UCLA).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-UCLAHonorDinner2006_11_06-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-5)

In sixth grade, Morhaime, along with his brother and sister, purchased a video game console called the [Bally Professional Arcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bally_Professional_Arcade "Bally Professional Arcade"), first released in 1978. Morhaime discovered that the console was programmable, and he taught himself how to write simple games on it, building off of example programming code he found in a gaming newsletter.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-latimes_interview-6)

As an electrical engineering student at UCLA, Morhaime focused more on [hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_hardware "Computer hardware") than on [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software "Software"). "I procrastinated a lot," he admitted.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-latimes_interview-6) Things changed after he got an internship at a [San Jose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California") microchip company. In his internship there, he learned about circuit design, and when he returned to school he was ahead of his computer architecture class. "I used to be the guy that sat in the back," he said, but after his stint in [Silicon Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Valley "Silicon Valley"), he said, "I started sitting up front."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-latimes_interview-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Blizzard Entertainment

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Blizzard Entertainment")]

While at UCLA, Morhaime bonded with [Allen Adham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Adham "Allen Adham") after realizing they shared the computer password "Joe". Upon graduating, Adham persuaded Morhaime into forgoing his job offer at [Western Digital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Digital "Western Digital") to instead found Silicon & Synapse in February 1991, later renamed [Blizzard Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blizzard_Entertainment "Blizzard Entertainment").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-7) After hiring their friend and fellow UCLA alumnus, Frank Pearce, they rented a small office in [Irvine, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_California "Irvine, California"), hoping to benefit from nearby technology companies.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-latimes_interview-6)

In 1995, Blizzard released _[Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft\_II:\_Tides\_of\_Darkness "Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness")_, its first number one selling game. "It's probably the game that put Blizzard on the map," Morhaime said. Besides its large number of sales, "it was the first game you could play over the Internet with a good experience," which was a novelty at the time, as well as being a defining selling point for its later titles.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-latimes_interview-6)

In planning for the release of _[World of Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_of\_Warcraft "World of Warcraft")_ (_WoW_) in late 2004, Morhaime thought that the market for the much larger and more interactive new game, the first in their history to require players to pay a monthly subscription fee, would grow slowly. "We felt it was very likely the fee would be a deterrent for people, and that _WoW_ would not sell as quickly as some of our previous games," he said. All of Blizzard's production and marketing decisions were based on that assumption. To Blizzard's surprise, _WoW_ sold extremely quickly, leaving the underprepared Blizzard unable to keep merchants supplied with the game for a short time. "For the whole first year, we scrambled to keep up with demand," he said. "It probably took years off of our lives." _World of Warcraft_ had approximately 11 million subscribers as of 2010. In 2017, Morhaime earned $12.3 million as the CEO of Blizzard.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-8)

On October 3, 2018, Morhaime announced he was stepping down as the company president and CEO, instead becoming an advisor to the company. Morhaime was replaced by J. Allen Brack, the executive producer on _World of Warcraft_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-9) His advisory role concluded on April 7, 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-10)

### Dreamhaven

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Dreamhaven")]

In 2020, Morhaime founded [Dreamhaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamhaven "Dreamhaven"), a video game company based in Irvine, California, with two internal studios: Secret Door and Moonshot Games.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-13)

In 2025, Dreamhaven published its first internally developed titles: **Sunderfolk**, a cooperative tactical RPG by Secret Door released on April 23 across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-14) and **Wildgate**, a crew‑based space‑shooter by Moonshot Games, which launched on July 22 on Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-15)

## Controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Controversy")]

Following Morhaime's departure from Blizzard, in July 2021, the [California Civil Rights Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Civil_Rights_Department "California Civil Rights Department") (CRD) (formerly known as the Department of Fair Employment and Housing) filed a lawsuit against Activision Blizzard for sexual harassment and gender-based discrimination in relation to unequal pay and retaliation against female employees in the workplace.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-16)

Amidst the news of the lawsuit, former Blizzard employees spoke out about their experiences and the harassment they witnessed within the company. A former manager at the then-competitive gaming brand FXOpen Esports, posted to social media about her experience at a Blizzard holiday party in which a senior creative director kissed her in front of a group of Blizzard employees, including Morhaime who was president and CEO at the time.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-18) While he was not named in the lawsuit, and some employees were uncertain whether he was aware of the allegations, multiple employees confirmed that Morhaime was present at some of the company events where the alleged misconduct took place. Morhaime tweeted an apology saying he was “ashamed” regarding the lawsuit several days after the news broke.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-20)

## Honors and awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Honors and awards")]

In 2008, Morhaime was inducted into the [Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences' Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Interactive_Arts_and_Sciences'_Hall_of_Fame "Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences' Hall of Fame").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-21) On the same year, Morhaime was honored at the 59th Annual [Technology & Engineering Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technology_&_Engineering_Emmy_Award "Technology & Engineering Emmy Award") for Blizzard's creation of _[World of Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_of\_Warcraft "World of Warcraft")_. Along with [Don Daglow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Daglow "Don Daglow") of [Stormfront Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormfront_Studios "Stormfront Studios") and [John Carmack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_D._Carmack "John D. Carmack") of [id Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Id_Software "Id Software"), Morhaime is one of only three designers or producers to accept awards at the Technology & Engineering Emmy Awards and at the [Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Interactive_Arts_&_Sciences "Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences")[Interactive Achievement Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interactive_Achievement_Awards "Interactive Achievement Awards").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-22)

Morhaime received the national [Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young_Entrepreneur_of_the_Year_Award "Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year Award") in the Technology category in 2012.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-23) In 2019, Morhaime was appointed the 2019 Honor Award at the Gamelab Barcelona, in Spain for his success in the gaming industry.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-24)

## Multimedia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Multimedia")]

In 2012, Morhaime made a cameo appearance on _[The Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guild\_(web\_series) "The Guild (web series)")_, a web series about the lives of a gamers' online experiences with an MMORPG that draws references to _World of Warcraft_. He is known for his work with the gaming community, but also worked on the 2016 film _[Warcraft: The Beginning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft:\_The\_Beginning "Warcraft: The Beginning")_.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Morhaime&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Michael_Morhaime_and_Dave_Berggren_playing_with_L80ETC_at_BlizzCon_2009.jpg/250px-Michael_Morhaime_and_Dave_Berggren_playing_with_L80ETC_at_BlizzCon_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Morhaime_and_Dave_Berggren_playing_with_L80ETC_at_BlizzCon_2009.jpg)

Morhaime (left) playing with ETC at BlizzCon 2009

In 2010, Morhaime married his long-time girlfriend Amy Chen.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-wapo-1)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-25) In 2017, Morhaime bought a mansion in a gated [Rancho Mirage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Mirage,_California "Rancho Mirage, California") community in [Riverside County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_County,_California "Riverside County, California"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") for $2.25 million.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-26) He is a member of Elite Tauren Chieftain, a [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band formed of and by Blizzard employees, where he plays [bass guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_guitar "Bass guitar").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morhaime#cite_note-27)
