**Mark Jonathan Pincus** (born February 13, 1966)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-3) is an American Internet [entrepreneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneur "Entrepreneur") known as the founder of [Zynga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga "Zynga"), a mobile social gaming company. Pincus also founded the startups Freeloader, Inc., [Tribe Networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribe.net "Tribe.net"), and [Support.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support.com "Support.com").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-become-4) Pincus was the CEO of Zynga until July 2013, then again from 2015 to 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-5)

Pincus was named 2009 "CEO of the Year"[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-6) at [The Crunchies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crunchies "Crunchies") technology awards[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-7) and a year later was named Founder of the Year at the 2010 ceremony.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-8) Zynga is considered to be the pioneer of the social gaming industry.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Seeking_Alpha_12.12-9) In 2011, Zynga went public with a $1 billion [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-CNNMoney_7.11-10) Pincus co-founded Reinvent Capital in 2018, an investment firm, with [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman") and [hedge fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund "Hedge fund") manager Michael Thompson.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-12) He co-created the [Stanford Graduate School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Graduate_School_of_Business "Stanford Graduate School of Business") course on Product Management with Professor Amir Goldberg.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-13)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Pincus' family lived in the [Lincoln Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Park,_Chicago "Lincoln Park, Chicago") neighborhood of [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). He is the son of Donna (née Forman) and Theodore Pincus,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-SunTimesTheodore-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-15) and is [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Jews "American Jews").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-16) His father was a business columnist and public relations adviser to CEOs and politicians,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-17) and his mother was an artist and [architect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architect "Architect").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-18)

Pincus attended [Francis W. Parker School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_W._Parker_School_(Chicago) "Francis W. Parker School (Chicago)") from kindergarten through 12th grade and graduated in 1984.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-19) He graduated _summa cum laude_ with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-20) from the [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School") of the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") earned in 1988[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-21) and an [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBA "MBA") from [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-22) where he founded the Communications Club with [Sherry Coutu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherry_Coutu "Sherry Coutu").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-23)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Financial services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Financial services")]

Before he became an entrepreneur, Pincus worked in venture capital and financial services for six years. After graduating from Wharton, Pincus spent two years working as an analyst in the New Media Group at [Lazard Freres & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazard_Freres_&_Co. "Lazard Freres & Co.")[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-CNBC:_Mark_Pincus-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Vanity_Fair:_Ol'_Mark_Pincus_Had_a_Farm-25) After that time, he moved to Hong Kong, where he was a Vice President for Asian Capital Partners for two years.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:1-27)

He returned to the United States in order to attend Harvard Business School (HBS) where he was a contemporary of [Chris Hohn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hohn "Chris Hohn"), [Guy Spier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Spier "Guy Spier")[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-28) and [Chris Shumway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Robertson "Julian Robertson").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:0-29) He graduated in 1993[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-30) and also spent a summer as an associate for [Bain & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bain_&_Co. "Bain & Co.") in 1992.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-31)

After Pincus graduated from Harvard Business School, he took a job as a manager of corporate development at [Tele-Communications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tele-Communications "Tele-Communications"), Inc., which is now AT&T Cable.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-32) A year later, he joined Columbia Capital as vice president, where he led investments in new media and software startups in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") for a year.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-33)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:0-29)

### Entrepreneur

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Entrepreneur")]

#### Freeloader

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Freeloader")]

In 1995, Pincus co-founded his first startup, Freeloader, Inc with Sunil Paul.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-34) Freeloader was backed by [Fred Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Wilson_(financier) "Fred Wilson (financier)") and [Softbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoftBank_Capital "SoftBank Capital").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-35) The company was acquired seven months after its launch by Individual, Inc., for $38 million.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-36)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:1-27)[Sean Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker "Sean Parker") worked as a summer intern at Freeloader when he was 14 years old. He later went on to co-found [Napster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napster "Napster"), and Pincus became Napster's first investor with an investment of $100,000.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-38)

#### Support.com

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Support.com")]

He then started his second company, Support.com, in August 1997. As Chairman and CEO, Pincus built the company into a leading provider of [help desk software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_desk_software "Help desk software"). The company went public in July 2000 at a $1.5 billion valuation.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-39) In 2002, the company changed its name from Support.com to SupportSoft, Inc.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-40)

#### Tribe.net

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Tribe.net")]

In 2003, at age 37, Pincus founded his third startup, Tribe.net, an early social network.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-GigaOM_3.2007-41) Tribe.net partnered with major local newspapers and was backed by [The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post"), [Knight Ridder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_Ridder "Knight Ridder") Digital, and Mayfield Fund and [Guy Spier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Spier "Guy Spier"),. In 2007, [Cisco Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco_Systems "Cisco Systems") acquired the core technology of Tribe.net to develop a social networking platform for its digital media services group.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-42)

In 2003, Pincus and [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman") purchased the [Six Degrees patent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Degrees_patent "Six Degrees patent"), a broad, sweeping patent that describes a social network service that is the heart of social networks from the extinct Sixdegrees.com company for $700,000.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-44) Pincus and Hoffman stated at the time that their objective in buying the patent was to protect innovation in social networking and to prevent large companies from interfering with this.

#### Investing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Investing")]

Pincus was a founding investor in [Napster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napster "Napster"), [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Friendster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendster "Friendster"), [Snapchat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapchat "Snapchat"), [Xiaomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiaomi "Xiaomi") and [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-All_Things_D_video-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-NYT_Times_1.2005-46) He was also an early investor in [JD.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD.com "JD.com"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-47)[Brightmail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brightmail "Brightmail") (later acquired by [Symantec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NortonLifeLock "NortonLifeLock") for $400m),[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-48) and Buddy Media (acquired by [Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce.com "Salesforce.com") for $800m).[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-49) In 2015, Pincus invested in the [nootropics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nootropics "Nootropics") company HVMN (formerly [Nootrobox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nootrobox "Nootrobox")),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-52) man-made diamond company Diamond Foundry,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-53) and in 2014 automated investment service firm Wealthfront.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-54)

#### Zynga

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Zynga")]

Main article: [Zynga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga "Zynga")

In July 2007 Pincus founded his fourth company, Zynga Inc., named after his deceased [American bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_bulldog "American bulldog") Zinga.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-58) Zynga developed games on top of social networks such as Facebook, [Myspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myspace "Myspace"), and [Bebo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bebo "Bebo").

In 2011, Pincus took the company public with a $1 billion IPO.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-59) Pincus was CEO of the company from 2007 to 2013.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-60) On July 1, 2013, Zynga recruited [Don Mattrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Mattrick "Don Mattrick"), the former president of Interactive Entertainment Business at [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), to succeed Pincus as CEO.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-61) Pincus remained actively involved in the company as Chairman of the Board and Chief Product Officer,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-62) but stepped down from his role as chief product officer to focus on his role as chairman of the board, the company announced in April 2014.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-King-2)

Pincus returned to the role of CEO of Zynga in April 2015.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-63) On March 7, 2016, Pincus stepped down as CEO, but continued his association with Zynga as Executive Chairman of the Board with [Frank Gibeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Gibeau?action=edit&redlink=1 "Frank Gibeau (page does not exist)") in the role of CEO.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-64) In 2018, citing his confidence in Zynga's management, Pincus voluntarily reduced his voting rights in the company from 70% to 10% and stepped back to a non-executive chairman role _._[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-67)

### Start-ups

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Start-ups")]

In 2014 Pincus started Superlabs, an incubator to develop products. Zynga acquired Superlabs in 2015.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-69)

In 2017, Pincus, alongside Reid Hoffman and [Adam Werbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Werbach "Adam Werbach"), launched [Win the Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Win_the_Future_(group) "Win the Future (group)"), a movement within the Democratic Party.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-71)

### Reinvent Capital and SPACs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reinvent Capital and SPACs")]

In 2018, with [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman") and Michael Thompson, Pincus co-founded Reinvent Capital, an investment firm that invests in internet, software, and media companies.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-72) Reinvent Capital has made investments in [Zipline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipline_(drone_delivery) "Zipline (drone delivery)"), [goPuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopuff "Gopuff"),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-73)[Dataminr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dataminr "Dataminr"),[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-74) Nimble Robotics,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-75)[Oscar Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Health "Oscar Health"),[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-76)[Lyft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyft "Lyft"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:2-77) all.Health, [Convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_(company) "Convoy (company)"),[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-78)[SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:2-77) and [Aurora Innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Innovation "Aurora Innovation").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-79)

In September 2020, Reinvent launched Reinvent Technology Partners (RTP), a [special purpose acquisition company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special-purpose_acquisition_company "Special-purpose acquisition company") (SPAC) which raised $690 million in its IPO.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-82) In February 2021, RTP announced a merger with [electronic vertical take-off and landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EVTOL "EVTOL") aircraft pioneer [Joby Aviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joby_Aviation "Joby Aviation"), valuing the company at $5 billion.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-83) Other investors included [Uber Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uber "Uber"), The [Baupost Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baupost_Group "Baupost Group"), [BlackRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackRock "BlackRock"), [Fidelity Management & Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidelity_Investments "Fidelity Investments"), and [Baillie Gifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baillie_Gifford "Baillie Gifford").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-84)

In November 2020, the group launched its second SPAC, Reinvent Technology Partners Z, which raised $230 million in its IPO.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-85) In March 2021, RTPZ announced a merger with insurance technology company [Hippo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippo_(company) "Hippo (company)") Insurance.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-86) Hippo provides home insurance in the United States, and uses artificial intelligence and big data to aggregate and analyze property information.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-89)

In February 2021, Pincus and Reinvent partners announced its third SPAC, Reinvent Technology Partners Y, raising $977.5 million in its IPO.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-90) In July 2021, RTPY announced a plan to merge with Pittsburgh-based [Aurora Innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Innovation "Aurora Innovation"), which is developing Level 4 self-driving technology for trucks and passenger vehicles.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-91)

## Philanthropy and community service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Philanthropy and community service")]

### Presidio Trust

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Presidio Trust")]

Pincus is a former member[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-92) of the board of the [Presidio Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidio_of_San_Francisco "Presidio of San Francisco"), a federal agency that operates and maintains the Presidio as part of the Golden Gate Recreation Area.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-93) He was appointed to the board by [President Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") in 2017.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-94)

### Zynga.org

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Zynga.org")]

In October 2009, Pincus started [Zynga.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga.org "Zynga.org"). [Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20100717174308/http://www.web2summit.com/web2010/public/schedule/speakers/) 2010-07-17 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine"). Web 2 Summit. Retrieved on 2011-11-13. Zynga.org has since raised more than $20 million[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Zynga_Blog_1.2013-95) for more than 50 international nonprofits[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-97) by occasionally selling virtual goods for charitable causes.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-techcrunch.com-98) During his time at Zynga Pincus created features for several gaming sites that allowed players to donate to the [San Francisco Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_the_Prevention_of_Cruelty_to_Animals "Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals") (SPCA); two organizations in [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"), FATEM and [Fonkoze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fonkoze "Fonkoze"), raising $427,000 in less than three weeks in October 2009. In January 2010 Zynga.org had raised $1.5 million in five days for [Haiti Earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake") relief. The money was distributed within just two days.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-99) The total Zynga.org raised during 2010 for earthquake relief in Haiti was $3 million. In 2011 they raised an additional $2 million for rescue efforts in Japan after the earthquake and tsunami that devastated the country.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-100)

On March 11, 2011, Zynga announced that 100 percent of the proceeds from the purchase of virtual goods from more than seven of its games would go toward Japan's [Save the Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_the_Children "Save the Children") Earthquake Emergency Fund.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-102) During the 2012 holiday season, Zynga.org partnered with [Toys for Tots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toys_for_Tots "Toys for Tots") in its largest charitable campaign not related to disaster relief. The campaign raised $745,000, with 100 percent of the purchase price of certain virtual goods going to Toys for Tots.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Zynga_Blog_1.2013-95)

In 2014, Zynga raised $1 million for [Water.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water.org "Water.org"), a [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri")-based charity that funds clean water projects in developing countries.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-103)

### Zynga match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Zynga match")]

Zynga announced in June 2020 that they created a $25 million fund to invest in charitable causes and educational organizations that promote diversity and inclusion.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-105)

### Oakland Undivided Campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Oakland Undivided Campaign")]

In May 2020, Pincus donated $700,000 to the [Oakland Unified School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Unified_School_District "Oakland Unified School District") and City of [Oakland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California") to help meet their $12.5 million goal towards eliminating the prevalent [digital gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_divide "Digital divide") that exists in Oakland.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-108)

### Roden Crater Project

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Roden Crater Project")]

In February 2020, Pincus donated $3 million to [Roden Crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roden_Crater "Roden Crater"), a large scale Land artwork by [James Turrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Turrell "James Turrell") within a dormant volcano in the Painted Desert region of Northern Arizona. The contributions bring the project closer to completion which the artist hopes to open within the next five years.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-109)

### Bolinas COVID-19 testing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Bolinas COVID-19 testing")]

In April 2020, Pincus, Finnish entrepreneur [Jyri Engeström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaiku "Jaiku") and biotech executive Cyrus Harmon, organized and financed community-wide COVID-19 testing in their hometown of [Bolinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolinas "Bolinas"), California. It was one of the first cases of community-wide testing in the US.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-110) Through their efforts Bolinas was able to test every one of its 1,600 residents for COVID-19 for free. Pincus donated the first $100,000 for the initiative, since it was not covered by government funds.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-111)

### Canal Alliance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Canal Alliance")]

Pincus donated over $100,000 to Canal Alliance in June 2020. Canal Alliance is a nonprofit champion of immigrants who are challenged by a lack of resources and an unfamiliar environment.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-112)

## Political views

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Political views")]

Pincus describes his views as libertarian.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:3-113) He co-hosted a fundraiser for [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris")'s 2016 Senate campaign[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-114) and in 2020, along with many other Silicon Valley tech billionaires, gave the legal maximum dollar amount to support [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden")'s presidential campaign.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-115) In July 2024, Pincus wrote that "Biden looks even riskier than Trump," disagreed with calls for Harris to replace Biden on the Democratic ticket, and praised aspects of Donald Trump's presidency.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:3-113)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 2008, Pincus married Alison Gelb, who founded [One Kings Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Kings_Lane "One Kings Lane"), a furniture and home accessories sales website that was sold to [Bed Bath & Beyond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bed_Bath_&_Beyond_Inc. "Bed Bath & Beyond Inc.") in 2016. They have three children, twin girls and a boy, and live in the [Pacific Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Heights "Pacific Heights") neighborhood of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-116) In March 2017, the couple divorced.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-117)

Pincus spends his time away from work with his daughters, cycling,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-The_San_Diego_Union-Tribune:_CEO_Interview:_Zynga's_Mark_Pincus,_unleashed-118) surfing, playing soccer[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Gadgets_360:_In_conversation_with_Mark_Pincus,_CEO_Zynga-119) and doing yoga.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Vanity_Fair:_OL%E2%80%99_MARK_PINCUS_HAD_A_FARM%E2%80%A6-120)

He joined [The Giving Pledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Giving_Pledge "The Giving Pledge") in 2022, committing to donating most of his wealth.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-121)

**Mark Jonathan Pincus** (born February 13, 1966)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-3) is an American Internet [entrepreneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneur "Entrepreneur") known as the founder of [Zynga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga "Zynga"), a mobile social gaming company. Pincus also founded the startups Freeloader, Inc., [Tribe Networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribe.net "Tribe.net"), and [Support.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support.com "Support.com").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-become-4) Pincus was the CEO of Zynga until July 2013, then again from 2015 to 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-5)

Pincus was named 2009 "CEO of the Year"[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-6) at [The Crunchies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crunchies "Crunchies") technology awards[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-7) and a year later was named Founder of the Year at the 2010 ceremony.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-8) Zynga is considered to be the pioneer of the social gaming industry.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Seeking_Alpha_12.12-9) In 2011, Zynga went public with a $1 billion [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-CNNMoney_7.11-10) Pincus co-founded Reinvent Capital in 2018, an investment firm, with [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman") and [hedge fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund "Hedge fund") manager Michael Thompson.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-12) He co-created the [Stanford Graduate School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Graduate_School_of_Business "Stanford Graduate School of Business") course on Product Management with Professor Amir Goldberg.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-13)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Pincus' family lived in the [Lincoln Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Park,_Chicago "Lincoln Park, Chicago") neighborhood of [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). He is the son of Donna (née Forman) and Theodore Pincus,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-SunTimesTheodore-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-15) and is [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Jews "American Jews").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-16) His father was a business columnist and public relations adviser to CEOs and politicians,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-17) and his mother was an artist and [architect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architect "Architect").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-18)

Pincus attended [Francis W. Parker School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_W._Parker_School_(Chicago) "Francis W. Parker School (Chicago)") from kindergarten through 12th grade and graduated in 1984.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-19) He graduated _summa cum laude_ with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-20) from the [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School") of the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") earned in 1988[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-21) and an [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBA "MBA") from [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-22) where he founded the Communications Club with [Sherry Coutu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherry_Coutu "Sherry Coutu").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-23)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Financial services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Financial services")]

Before he became an entrepreneur, Pincus worked in venture capital and financial services for six years. After graduating from Wharton, Pincus spent two years working as an analyst in the New Media Group at [Lazard Freres & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazard_Freres_&_Co. "Lazard Freres & Co.")[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-CNBC:_Mark_Pincus-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Vanity_Fair:_Ol'_Mark_Pincus_Had_a_Farm-25) After that time, he moved to Hong Kong, where he was a Vice President for Asian Capital Partners for two years.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:1-27)

He returned to the United States in order to attend Harvard Business School (HBS) where he was a contemporary of [Chris Hohn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hohn "Chris Hohn"), [Guy Spier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Spier "Guy Spier")[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-28) and [Chris Shumway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Robertson "Julian Robertson").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:0-29) He graduated in 1993[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-30) and also spent a summer as an associate for [Bain & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bain_&_Co. "Bain & Co.") in 1992.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-31)

After Pincus graduated from Harvard Business School, he took a job as a manager of corporate development at [Tele-Communications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tele-Communications "Tele-Communications"), Inc., which is now AT&T Cable.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-32) A year later, he joined Columbia Capital as vice president, where he led investments in new media and software startups in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") for a year.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-33)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:0-29)

### Entrepreneur

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Entrepreneur")]

#### Freeloader

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Freeloader")]

In 1995, Pincus co-founded his first startup, Freeloader, Inc with Sunil Paul.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-34) Freeloader was backed by [Fred Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Wilson_(financier) "Fred Wilson (financier)") and [Softbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoftBank_Capital "SoftBank Capital").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-35) The company was acquired seven months after its launch by Individual, Inc., for $38 million.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-36)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:1-27)[Sean Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Parker "Sean Parker") worked as a summer intern at Freeloader when he was 14 years old. He later went on to co-found [Napster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napster "Napster"), and Pincus became Napster's first investor with an investment of $100,000.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-38)

#### Support.com

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Support.com")]

He then started his second company, Support.com, in August 1997. As Chairman and CEO, Pincus built the company into a leading provider of [help desk software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_desk_software "Help desk software"). The company went public in July 2000 at a $1.5 billion valuation.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-39) In 2002, the company changed its name from Support.com to SupportSoft, Inc.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-40)

#### Tribe.net

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Tribe.net")]

In 2003, at age 37, Pincus founded his third startup, Tribe.net, an early social network.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-GigaOM_3.2007-41) Tribe.net partnered with major local newspapers and was backed by [The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post"), [Knight Ridder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_Ridder "Knight Ridder") Digital, and Mayfield Fund and [Guy Spier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Spier "Guy Spier"),. In 2007, [Cisco Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco_Systems "Cisco Systems") acquired the core technology of Tribe.net to develop a social networking platform for its digital media services group.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-42)

In 2003, Pincus and [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman") purchased the [Six Degrees patent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Degrees_patent "Six Degrees patent"), a broad, sweeping patent that describes a social network service that is the heart of social networks from the extinct Sixdegrees.com company for $700,000.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-44) Pincus and Hoffman stated at the time that their objective in buying the patent was to protect innovation in social networking and to prevent large companies from interfering with this.

#### Investing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Investing")]

Pincus was a founding investor in [Napster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napster "Napster"), [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Friendster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendster "Friendster"), [Snapchat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapchat "Snapchat"), [Xiaomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiaomi "Xiaomi") and [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-All_Things_D_video-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-NYT_Times_1.2005-46) He was also an early investor in [JD.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD.com "JD.com"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-47)[Brightmail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brightmail "Brightmail") (later acquired by [Symantec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NortonLifeLock "NortonLifeLock") for $400m),[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-48) and Buddy Media (acquired by [Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce.com "Salesforce.com") for $800m).[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-49) In 2015, Pincus invested in the [nootropics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nootropics "Nootropics") company HVMN (formerly [Nootrobox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nootrobox "Nootrobox")),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-52) man-made diamond company Diamond Foundry,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-53) and in 2014 automated investment service firm Wealthfront.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-54)

#### Zynga

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Zynga")]

Main article: [Zynga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga "Zynga")

In July 2007 Pincus founded his fourth company, Zynga Inc., named after his deceased [American bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_bulldog "American bulldog") Zinga.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-58) Zynga developed games on top of social networks such as Facebook, [Myspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myspace "Myspace"), and [Bebo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bebo "Bebo").

In 2011, Pincus took the company public with a $1 billion IPO.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-59) Pincus was CEO of the company from 2007 to 2013.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-60) On July 1, 2013, Zynga recruited [Don Mattrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Mattrick "Don Mattrick"), the former president of Interactive Entertainment Business at [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), to succeed Pincus as CEO.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-61) Pincus remained actively involved in the company as Chairman of the Board and Chief Product Officer,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-62) but stepped down from his role as chief product officer to focus on his role as chairman of the board, the company announced in April 2014.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-King-2)

Pincus returned to the role of CEO of Zynga in April 2015.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-63) On March 7, 2016, Pincus stepped down as CEO, but continued his association with Zynga as Executive Chairman of the Board with [Frank Gibeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Gibeau?action=edit&redlink=1 "Frank Gibeau (page does not exist)") in the role of CEO.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-64) In 2018, citing his confidence in Zynga's management, Pincus voluntarily reduced his voting rights in the company from 70% to 10% and stepped back to a non-executive chairman role _._[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-67)

### Start-ups

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Start-ups")]

In 2014 Pincus started Superlabs, an incubator to develop products. Zynga acquired Superlabs in 2015.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-69)

In 2017, Pincus, alongside Reid Hoffman and [Adam Werbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Werbach "Adam Werbach"), launched [Win the Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Win_the_Future_(group) "Win the Future (group)"), a movement within the Democratic Party.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-71)

### Reinvent Capital and SPACs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reinvent Capital and SPACs")]

In 2018, with [Reid Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Hoffman "Reid Hoffman") and Michael Thompson, Pincus co-founded Reinvent Capital, an investment firm that invests in internet, software, and media companies.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-72) Reinvent Capital has made investments in [Zipline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipline_(drone_delivery) "Zipline (drone delivery)"), [goPuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopuff "Gopuff"),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-73)[Dataminr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dataminr "Dataminr"),[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-74) Nimble Robotics,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-75)[Oscar Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Health "Oscar Health"),[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-76)[Lyft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyft "Lyft"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:2-77) all.Health, [Convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_(company) "Convoy (company)"),[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-78)[SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:2-77) and [Aurora Innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Innovation "Aurora Innovation").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-79)

In September 2020, Reinvent launched Reinvent Technology Partners (RTP), a [special purpose acquisition company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special-purpose_acquisition_company "Special-purpose acquisition company") (SPAC) which raised $690 million in its IPO.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-82) In February 2021, RTP announced a merger with [electronic vertical take-off and landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EVTOL "EVTOL") aircraft pioneer [Joby Aviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joby_Aviation "Joby Aviation"), valuing the company at $5 billion.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-83) Other investors included [Uber Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uber "Uber"), The [Baupost Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baupost_Group "Baupost Group"), [BlackRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackRock "BlackRock"), [Fidelity Management & Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidelity_Investments "Fidelity Investments"), and [Baillie Gifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baillie_Gifford "Baillie Gifford").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-84)

In November 2020, the group launched its second SPAC, Reinvent Technology Partners Z, which raised $230 million in its IPO.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-85) In March 2021, RTPZ announced a merger with insurance technology company [Hippo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippo_(company) "Hippo (company)") Insurance.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-86) Hippo provides home insurance in the United States, and uses artificial intelligence and big data to aggregate and analyze property information.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-89)

In February 2021, Pincus and Reinvent partners announced its third SPAC, Reinvent Technology Partners Y, raising $977.5 million in its IPO.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-90) In July 2021, RTPY announced a plan to merge with Pittsburgh-based [Aurora Innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Innovation "Aurora Innovation"), which is developing Level 4 self-driving technology for trucks and passenger vehicles.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-91)

## Philanthropy and community service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Philanthropy and community service")]

### Presidio Trust

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Presidio Trust")]

Pincus is a former member[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-92) of the board of the [Presidio Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidio_of_San_Francisco "Presidio of San Francisco"), a federal agency that operates and maintains the Presidio as part of the Golden Gate Recreation Area.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-93) He was appointed to the board by [President Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") in 2017.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-94)

### Zynga.org

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Zynga.org")]

In October 2009, Pincus started [Zynga.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga.org "Zynga.org"). [Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20100717174308/http://www.web2summit.com/web2010/public/schedule/speakers/) 2010-07-17 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine"). Web 2 Summit. Retrieved on 2011-11-13. Zynga.org has since raised more than $20 million[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Zynga_Blog_1.2013-95) for more than 50 international nonprofits[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-97) by occasionally selling virtual goods for charitable causes.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-techcrunch.com-98) During his time at Zynga Pincus created features for several gaming sites that allowed players to donate to the [San Francisco Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_the_Prevention_of_Cruelty_to_Animals "Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals") (SPCA); two organizations in [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"), FATEM and [Fonkoze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fonkoze "Fonkoze"), raising $427,000 in less than three weeks in October 2009. In January 2010 Zynga.org had raised $1.5 million in five days for [Haiti Earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake") relief. The money was distributed within just two days.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-99) The total Zynga.org raised during 2010 for earthquake relief in Haiti was $3 million. In 2011 they raised an additional $2 million for rescue efforts in Japan after the earthquake and tsunami that devastated the country.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-100)

On March 11, 2011, Zynga announced that 100 percent of the proceeds from the purchase of virtual goods from more than seven of its games would go toward Japan's [Save the Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_the_Children "Save the Children") Earthquake Emergency Fund.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-102) During the 2012 holiday season, Zynga.org partnered with [Toys for Tots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toys_for_Tots "Toys for Tots") in its largest charitable campaign not related to disaster relief. The campaign raised $745,000, with 100 percent of the purchase price of certain virtual goods going to Toys for Tots.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Zynga_Blog_1.2013-95)

In 2014, Zynga raised $1 million for [Water.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water.org "Water.org"), a [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri")-based charity that funds clean water projects in developing countries.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-103)

### Zynga match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Zynga match")]

Zynga announced in June 2020 that they created a $25 million fund to invest in charitable causes and educational organizations that promote diversity and inclusion.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-105)

### Oakland Undivided Campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Oakland Undivided Campaign")]

In May 2020, Pincus donated $700,000 to the [Oakland Unified School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Unified_School_District "Oakland Unified School District") and City of [Oakland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California") to help meet their $12.5 million goal towards eliminating the prevalent [digital gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_divide "Digital divide") that exists in Oakland.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-108)

### Roden Crater Project

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Roden Crater Project")]

In February 2020, Pincus donated $3 million to [Roden Crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roden_Crater "Roden Crater"), a large scale Land artwork by [James Turrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Turrell "James Turrell") within a dormant volcano in the Painted Desert region of Northern Arizona. The contributions bring the project closer to completion which the artist hopes to open within the next five years.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-109)

### Bolinas COVID-19 testing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Bolinas COVID-19 testing")]

In April 2020, Pincus, Finnish entrepreneur [Jyri Engeström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaiku "Jaiku") and biotech executive Cyrus Harmon, organized and financed community-wide COVID-19 testing in their hometown of [Bolinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolinas "Bolinas"), California. It was one of the first cases of community-wide testing in the US.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-110) Through their efforts Bolinas was able to test every one of its 1,600 residents for COVID-19 for free. Pincus donated the first $100,000 for the initiative, since it was not covered by government funds.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-111)

### Canal Alliance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Canal Alliance")]

Pincus donated over $100,000 to Canal Alliance in June 2020. Canal Alliance is a nonprofit champion of immigrants who are challenged by a lack of resources and an unfamiliar environment.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-112)

## Political views

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Political views")]

Pincus describes his views as libertarian.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:3-113) He co-hosted a fundraiser for [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris")'s 2016 Senate campaign[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-114) and in 2020, along with many other Silicon Valley tech billionaires, gave the legal maximum dollar amount to support [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden")'s presidential campaign.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-115) In July 2024, Pincus wrote that "Biden looks even riskier than Trump," disagreed with calls for Harris to replace Biden on the Democratic ticket, and praised aspects of Donald Trump's presidency.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-:3-113)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mark_Pincus&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 2008, Pincus married Alison Gelb, who founded [One Kings Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Kings_Lane "One Kings Lane"), a furniture and home accessories sales website that was sold to [Bed Bath & Beyond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bed_Bath_&_Beyond_Inc. "Bed Bath & Beyond Inc.") in 2016. They have three children, twin girls and a boy, and live in the [Pacific Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Heights "Pacific Heights") neighborhood of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-116) In March 2017, the couple divorced.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-117)

Pincus spends his time away from work with his daughters, cycling,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-The_San_Diego_Union-Tribune:_CEO_Interview:_Zynga's_Mark_Pincus,_unleashed-118) surfing, playing soccer[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Gadgets_360:_In_conversation_with_Mark_Pincus,_CEO_Zynga-119) and doing yoga.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-Vanity_Fair:_OL%E2%80%99_MARK_PINCUS_HAD_A_FARM%E2%80%A6-120)

He joined [The Giving Pledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Giving_Pledge "The Giving Pledge") in 2022, committing to donating most of his wealth.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pincus#cite_note-121)

**Zynga Inc.** ([/ˈ z ɪ ŋ ɡ ə/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")) is an American [video game developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_developer "Video game developer") and [publisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_publisher "Video game publisher") known for its [social video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_video_game "Social video game") services. It was founded in April 2007, and it is owned by [Take-Two Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take-Two_Interactive "Take-Two Interactive") since 2022, with headquarters in [San Mateo, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo,_California "San Mateo, California").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-sanmateo-hq-7) The company primarily focuses on mobile and social networking platforms.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Zynga-Feb-2018-10-K-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-About_Us_Zynga-9) Zynga states its mission as "connecting the world through games".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-10)

Zynga launched _[FarmVille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FarmVille "FarmVille")_ on Facebook in June 2009,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Zynga-Jul-2011-S-1-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-AllFacebook_FarmVille-11) reaching ten million daily active users (DAU) within six weeks.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Polygon_Fmville_2-12) As of August 2017, Zynga had thirty million monthly active users (MAU).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-13) In 2017, its most successful games were _[Zynga Poker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga\_Poker "Zynga Poker")_ and _[Words with Friends 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Words\_with\_Friends\_2 "Words with Friends 2")_, with about 57 million games being played at any given moment;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-15) and _CSR Racing 2_, the most popular [racing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_video_game "Racing video game") on mobile devices.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-16) Zynga began trading on [NASDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ") on December 16, 2011,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Forbes_IPO-17) under the ticker ZNGA.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Zynga-Dec-2011-S-1/A-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Zynga-Dec-2011-424B4-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-20)

[Take-Two Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take-Two_Interactive "Take-Two Interactive") announced in January 2022 its intent to buy Zynga for $12.7 billion.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-taketwo_acquire-21) The deal was completed in May 2022.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-22)

According to Take-Two Interactive, about 10% of the world's population plays Zynga's games every month.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-23)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zynga&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Zynga was founded in April 2007 by Mark Pincus,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-24) with founding team members [Eric Schiermeyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Schiermeyer "Eric Schiermeyer"), [Justin Waldron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Waldron "Justin Waldron"), Michael Luxton, Steve Schoettler, and Andrew Trader, under the name Presidio Media.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-25)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-takahashi-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-zynga-fact-sheet-4) The company name changed to Zynga in July 2007.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-takahashi-1)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-26) Zynga was named after Pincus' [American bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_bulldog "American bulldog") Zinga[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-shambora-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-poker-zinga-28) and uses an image of a bulldog as its logo. Zynga's first game, _Texas Hold 'Em Poker_, now known as _[Zynga Poker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga\_Poker "Zynga Poker")_, was released on Facebook in July 2007. It was the first game Facebook introduced on its social networking platform.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-29)

Zynga became the Facebook app developer with the most monthly active users in April 2009, with 40 million people playing its games that month.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-30) Soon after, the company opened its first external game studio in Baltimore, Zynga East, led by [Brian Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Reynolds_(game_designer) "Brian Reynolds (game designer)").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-32)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-33)

In June 2009, Zynga acquired MyMiniLife which built and launched _FarmVille_ on Facebook. By August, Farmville was the first game on Facebook to reach 10 million daily active users.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-34) On November 23, 2009, FarmVille.com went live as Zynga's first stand-alone game.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-35) In February 2010, Farmville had over 80 million players,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-36) and on May 18, 2010, Facebook and Zynga entered into a five-year relationship to expand the use of Facebook Credits in Zynga's games.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-37)

In December 2010, Zynga's game _[CityVille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CityVille "CityVille")_ surpassed _FarmVille_ as its most popular game[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-38) with over 61 million monthly active users and a base of over 16 million daily active users.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-39)

Zynga filed with the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") (SEC) to raise up to $1 billion in an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") on July 1, 2011. At the time, the company had 2,000 employees.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-s1reg-40) On November 28, 2011, the Finnish game developer [Rovio Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rovio_Entertainment "Rovio Entertainment") rejected an acquisition attempt from Zynga worth $2.25 billion.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-41) Zynga began trading on [NASDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ") on December 16, 2011.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-42)

Zynga acquired four game development companies, Game Doctors, developer of _Zombie Smash_, Page44 Studios, HipLogic and Astro Ape Studios.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-43) On June 26, 2012, during the Zynga Unleashed conference, Zynga announced the "Zynga With Friends" network, aiming to connect players of Zynga game titles across multiple platforms.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Wired_Unleashed_Report-44) Zynga also announced the Zynga API, intended to help developers build social games.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-ZDNet_API-45) The company announced that three new partners were developing games for Zynga.com including 50 Cubes, [Majesco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majesco "Majesco") and [Portalarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portalarium "Portalarium"). The company unveiled the Zynga Partners for Mobile program to help increase Zynga's presence on mobile devices.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-DMW-46)

In October 2012, Zynga announced a partnership with [bwin.party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bwin.Party_Digital_Entertainment "Bwin.Party Digital Entertainment"), an international real-money gaming operator, to launch real-money gaming in the UK,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Biz_Insider_Oct_2012-47) including the release of [online poker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_poker "Online poker"), a suite of 180 casino games, and the first online _FarmVille_-branded real money slots game during 2013.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Biz_Insider_Oct_2012-47)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Biz_Week_Oct_2012-48)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-CNNMoney_Q2-49)

On June 3, 2013, Zynga announced layoffs of 520 employees—roughly 18% of its workforce[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Zynga-Jun-2013-8-K-50)—and closed offices in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), and [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-51)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-52) By July 2013, Zynga had reportedly lost nearly half of its user base from the previous year. Consequently, investors decreased Zynga's valuation by $400 million.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-53) On July 25, 2013, Zynga said it would not be pursuing real money game production in the US.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Zynga-Jul-2013-8-K-54) Following this announcement, shares dropped 13%.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-55)

In July 2013, Zynga hired [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft")'s Interactive Entertainment President [Don Mattrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Mattrick "Don Mattrick") as its new CEO.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-56)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-57) Pincus remained as Zynga's chairman and [chief product officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_product_officer "Chief product officer").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-59)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Zynga_-_World_Cup.jpg/250px-Zynga_-_World_Cup.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zynga_-_World_Cup.jpg)

Employees watch the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") during a scheduled break.

In January 2014, the company announced the layoff of 314 workers, about 15% of its total workforce.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-60)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-61) In April 2014, founder & former CEO Pincus stepped down from his role as chief product officer. He remained as chairman of the board.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-62)

First quarter results for 2014 showed that daily active user numbers fell from 53 million to 28 million year-over-year.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-63) In April 2014, the company announced its new hire of Alex Garden, co-founder of [Relic Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relic_Entertainment "Relic Entertainment") and former [Microsoft Game Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Game_Studios "Microsoft Game Studios") executive.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-64)

In July 2014, Zynga signed a lease for office space in [Maitland, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maitland,_Florida "Maitland, Florida"). Less than one year later, this Orlando-area office was closed.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-65)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-66)

Don Mattrick left Zynga in April 2015, replaced by predecessor Mark Pincus.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-67) Frank Gibeau took over as CEO on March 7, 2016, with Pincus once again stepping aside. Gibeau's last position was as head of mobile for [Electronic Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Arts "Electronic Arts"). He joined Zynga's board of directors in August 2015.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-68)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-69)

Zynga headquarters in San Francisco in 2016

In the fourth quarter of 2017, revenue was $233.3 million, a 22% increase from the same quarter in 2016, the best quarterly performance in five years.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-70) As of January 2018, Zynga had 1,681 employees,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-71) approximately 80 million monthly active users,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-auto1-72) and a [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization") of $3.39 billion.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-73) According to the company, Zynga has had over one billion people play its games since its inception in 2007.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-74)

On January 10, 2022, [Take-Two Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take-Two_Interactive "Take-Two Interactive") announced its intention to acquire the company in a cash-and-stock deal with a value of $12.7 billion, with Take-Two acquiring all outstanding shares of Zynga at $9.86 apiece[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-taketwo_acquire-21) Both shareholders of the companies approved the merger on May 19, 2022, and the closing of the transaction took effect on May 23, 2022.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-75)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-76)

In June 2023, during the _[FTC v. Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTC\_v.\_Microsoft "FTC v. Microsoft")_ trial cross-examination, [Microsoft Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Gaming "Microsoft Gaming") CEO [Phil Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Spencer_(business_executive) "Phil Spencer (business executive)") disclosed that [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") considered purchasing Zynga before Take-Two Interactive acquired the studio in 2022.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-77)

## Funding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zynga&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Funding")]

In its first round of funding in January 2008, Zynga received US$10 million.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-78) In July of the same year, Zynga received US$29 million in [venture finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_finance "Venture finance") from several firms.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-79) During its first four years of operation Zynga raised a total of $854 million in three rounds of fund raising. The last round, in February 2011, raised $490 million.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-80)

### Public offering

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zynga&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Public offering")]

On July 1, 2011, the company filed its Form S-1 registration statement with the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") (SEC).[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-81) Zynga was priced at $10 per share and began trading on [NASDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ") under ZNGA on December 16, 2011. The stock closed down 5% on its first day,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-Forbes_IPO-17) then climbed 26% to $13.39 per share after Facebook's IPO filing on February 1, 2012 (Facebook had reported that 12% of its revenue comes from Zynga).[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-82) In March 2012 ZNGA was trading at $14.50.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-83) For several years the stock performed poorly, but in 2017 the price hit a three-year high. By the end of 2017 Zynga's shares were trading at $4.00, a 56% gain for the year.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zynga#cite_note-84)
