The **University of Central Florida** (**UCF**) is a [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university "Public university")[research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") with its main campus in unincorporated [Orange County, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_County,_Florida "Orange County, Florida"), near [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida"), United States. It is part of the [State University System of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_University_System_of_Florida "State University System of Florida"). With 70,674 students as of the fall 2025 semester, it has the [second-largest on-campus student body of any public university in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_public_university_campuses_by_enrollment "List of United States public university campuses by enrollment").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-UCFfacts2025-2026-2) UCF is classified among "[R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research spending and doctorate production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_research_universities_in_the_United_States "List of research universities in the United States")."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-8)

UCF was founded in 1963 and opened in 1968 as **Florida Technological University**. The new state university was intended in part to train scientists and engineers for the growing aerospace and defense workforce around [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") and what is now [Cape Canaveral Space Force Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Canaveral_Space_Force_Station "Cape Canaveral Space Force Station"). As the curriculum widened beyond engineering and the physical sciences, the school was renamed the University of Central Florida in 1978. It remains active in space-related research through units such as the [Florida Space Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Space_Institute "Florida Space Institute") and the NASA Florida Space Grant Consortium.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-9)

Most students attend the main campus, 13 miles (21 km) east of downtown Orlando. The university offers more than 230 degree programs through 13 colleges, including the Health Sciences Campus at [Lake Nona Medical City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Nona_Medical_City "Lake Nona Medical City"), the [Rosen College of Hospitality Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosen_College_of_Hospitality_Management "Rosen College of Hospitality Management"), and a campus in downtown Orlando. Since opening it has awarded more than 450,000 degrees.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-10)

The university's colors are black and gold. Its athletic teams, the [UCF Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCF_Knights "UCF Knights"), compete in [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") as members of the [Big 12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_12_Conference "Big 12 Conference").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-11)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Founding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Founding")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/13/FTU_Knights_logo.png/250px-FTU_Knights_logo.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FTU_Knights_logo.png)

The university's first Knights and Pegasus logo, used when the school was Florida Technological University

The Florida Legislature authorized a new public university in east-central Florida on June 10, 1963, when Governor [Farris Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farris_Bryant "Farris Bryant") signed Senate Bill No. 125.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-50history-12) Local officials had lobbied for the campus as the region’s population and the workforce around the [Space Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Coast "Space Coast") grew in the early 1960s. Former Senate President [William A. Shands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Shands "William A. Shands") and Senator [Beth Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beth_Johnson_(American_politician) "Beth Johnson (American politician)") were among the bill’s principal backers.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-50history-12) The university was founded as a [coeducational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed-sex_education "Mixed-sex education") state university with the mission of educating students for space-age careers in engineering and other technological professions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-50history-12)

On January 24, 1964, the [Florida Board of Regents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Board_of_Regents "Florida Board of Regents") bought 1,000 acres (400 ha) of undeveloped land along [Alafaya Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_434 "Florida State Road 434") in northeast Orange County for $500,000. Area residents later donated another 227 acres (92 ha) and helped raise more than $1 million toward the site.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-50history-12) In December 1965 the board appointed [Charles Millican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Millican "Charles Millican") as the university’s first president.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-13) After consulting a citizen advisory group, Millican selected the name Florida Technological University and helped design the Pegasus seal.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-14) He also introduced the motto “Reach for the Stars” and the paired slogans “accent on excellence” and “accent on the individual.” Millican laid out the main campus as a set of pedestrian rings inside a loop road, a plan later compared to mid-century planned-community design.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-millicanhonored-15)

Millican and Governor [Claude Kirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Kirk "Claude Kirk") broke ground in March 1967. Classes opened on October 7, 1968, with 1,948 students in 55 degree programs across five colleges, 90 instructors, and about 150 staff members.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-16) From the start the university drew students interested in engineering jobs tied to Kennedy Space Center and area defense contractors, but it opened with five colleges rather than as a federal laboratory school. The first graduating class, 423 students, received degrees on June 14, 1970. Astronaut and Orlando native [John Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Young_(astronaut) "John Young (astronaut)") spoke at commencement.

Millican chose the school colors. An early unofficial mascot, the [Citronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citronaut "Citronaut") — an orange-astronaut hybrid — did not last.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-17) After a short-lived “Vincent the Vulture” period, students in 1971 voted for the Knight of Pegasus as the athletic mascot. The teams later competed as the Golden Knights and then the Knights.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-mascot-18)

### Expansion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Expansion")]

Entering office in 1978, the university's second president, [Trevor Colbourn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Colbourn "Trevor Colbourn"), recognized the diversification and growth of UCF's academic programs away from its strictly technological and scientific beginnings.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-19) As the university developed strong business, education, and liberal arts programs, Colbourn recognized that the university's name no longer reflected its mission. From its establishment the university was known as Florida Technological University, nicknamed Florida Tech, until December 1978, when Governor [Reubin Askew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reubin_Askew "Reubin Askew") signed legislation changing the school's name to the University of Central Florida.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf-6)

Colbourn established the university's [honors program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnett_Honors_College "Burnett Honors College"), and started the university's first satellite campus[_[where?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Naming\_conventions\_(geographic\_names) "Wikipedia:Naming conventions (geographic names)")_]. In addition, he was responsible for constructing the [Central Florida Research Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Florida_Research_Park "Central Florida Research Park") adjacent to the UCF campus, founded in 1978. The park serves as a major focus of [simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulation "Simulation") for [space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_space "Outer space") and [defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_(military) "Defense (military)")-related research. It was part of Colbourn's plan to make UCF a world-class partnership university. Among the university's first partners were [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin") and the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy"), and Colbourn led the push to found both the [Institute for Simulation and Training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Simulation_and_Training "Institute for Simulation and Training") and the [Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Research_and_Education_in_Optics_and_Lasers "Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers") in 1986.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] During his tenure, enrollment increased from 11,000 in 1978 to over 18,000 in 1989.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-papers-20) Colbourn also supported the university's athletic programs. He was responsible for establishing the school's [football program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCF_Knights_football "UCF Knights football") in 1979, which began an era of growth for the university.[_[according to whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] In April 1979, UCF awarded its 15,000th degree.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Hitt presidency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Hitt presidency")]

In March 1992, [John C. Hitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C._Hitt "John C. Hitt") became UCF's fourth president. Once known mainly as a small commuter and technology school, UCF administrators began to increase its academic and research standing while also evolving into a more traditional research university. When Hitt took office, UCF's enrollment was 20,302. As of 2014, 60,821 students attended classes on 12 campuses spread across central Florida. The university consisted of 13 colleges and employed more than 10,150 faculty and staff.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf-6) During this time, UCF raised admissions standards, increased research funding, built new facilities, and established notable partnerships with major research institutions.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-21)

The university's athletic program also grew with an [on-campus football stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBC_Mortgage_Stadium "FBC Mortgage Stadium"), [new basketball arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addition_Financial_Arena "Addition Financial Arena"), more on-campus housing, and the development of the [UCF College of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_College_of_Medicine "University of Central Florida College of Medicine") at Lake Nona.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Until 1999, the Knights were represented by a [jouster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jousting "Jousting") from the [Medieval Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Times "Medieval Times") dinner show in nearby [Kissimmee, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kissimmee,_Florida "Kissimmee, Florida"). That same year, [Knightro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knightro "Knightro") was introduced at the staple homecoming event, Spirit Splash.

During its spring 2010 graduation ceremonies, UCF awarded its 200,000th degree,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-22) less than five years after awarding its 150,000th.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-23)

#### Colbourn Hall scandal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Colbourn Hall scandal")]

In August 2018, the state university system's [board of governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Board_of_Governors "Florida Board of Governors") and the [Florida legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_legislature "Florida legislature") opened an investigation into the university for misuse of state funds. On September 13, 2018, UCF admitted to misappropriating money intended for educational and operating expenses to build the new $38 million Trevor Colbourn Hall, leading to the resignation of CFO Bill Merck.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-24) In January 2019, UCF severed ties with President Emeritus John Hitt after the investigation proved that UCF had misspent or planned to misspend over $85 million between 2013 and 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-25) Newly appointed president [Dale Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Whittaker "Dale Whittaker"), who was a provost at UCF during Hitt's tenure, resigned in February 2019 after just seven months in office over allegations that he also knew about the misappropriation of funds.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-27) Board of trustees chairman Marcos Marchena also resigned that month.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-28) In August 2019, the final report into additional UCF construction projects revealed the balance of misdirected funds between July 2010 and August 2018 was $99.61 million (equivalent to $147.07 million in 2025).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-29) The report found that key people in the university leadership were aware of the misdirection of the funds. UCF was fined by the state for 120% the cost of the misused funds.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-30)

### Cartwright presidency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Cartwright presidency")]

[Alexander Cartwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Cartwright_(academic) "Alexander Cartwright (academic)") is the fifth and current president of UCF. He became the president on April 13, 2020, succeeding acting president Thad Seymore, who took over following Whittaker's resignation in February 2019.

## Campuses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Campuses")]

### Main campus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Main campus")]

The University of Central Florida main campus is located in the [University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University,_Orange_County,_Florida "University, Orange County, Florida")[census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place"),[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-31) along [Alafaya Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Road_434 "Florida State Road 434") east of [Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida"), Florida.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-32)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/UCF_Memory_Mall_%2830395273585%29.jpg/250px-UCF_Memory_Mall_%2830395273585%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCF_Memory_Mall_(30395273585).jpg)

Memory Mall

The campus is designed to be pedestrian-oriented, with a series of concentric circles.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The outermost circle is Gemini Blvd, which is also the main road for vehicular traffic on campus. Inside of Gemini, there is Apollo Circle, Mercury Circle, and finally Pegasus Circle as the innermost circle.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-33)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/UCF_Student_Union_%2830395278155%29.jpg/250px-UCF_Student_Union_%2830395278155%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCF_Student_Union_(30395278155).jpg)

Student Union

Pegasus Circle contains the student union, with the John C. Hitt Library located directly to the south of it. All academic buildings are located inside of Gemini, with the circle divided up into pie-shaped sections for each college.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-34) As there are very few roads inside of Gemini, many buildings' loading docks are accessible only by sidewalks and thus receive most deliveries at night.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The University of Central Florida campus is one of only two in the nation with a concentric circle design, the other being the University of California, Irvine.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-35)_Newsweek_ ranked UCF as having the 20th most beautiful university campus in the country in 2011.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-36)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/UCF_Tower.jpg/250px-UCF_Tower.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCF_Tower.jpg)

UCF Tower student housing dorms

Student housing is provided along the perimeter of the campus. Outside of Gemini, the campus is divided up into different themed sections.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The northwest side of campus includes Greek communities and on-campus residences.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Knights_Plaza.jpg/250px-Knights_Plaza.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Knights_Plaza.jpg)

East retail and Tower III at Knights Plaza

The north side contains [Knights Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_Plaza "Knights Plaza"), an uptown style athletic village with stores and restaurants, the east side contains the [Arboretum of the University of Central Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arboretum_of_the_University_of_Central_Florida "Arboretum of the University of Central Florida") and the engineering wing.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/UCF_Gym.jpg/250px-UCF_Gym.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCF_Gym.jpg)

UCF Recreation and Wellness Center

The south side contains student recreation and wellness facilities, leisure pool, recreation park, and more student housing. Also located directly south of the main campus is [Central Florida Research Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Florida_Research_Park "Central Florida Research Park"), which is the seventh largest research park in the nation and the largest in Florida,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-seventhpark-37) housing over 116 corporations. The park provides more than 10,000 jobs to over 500 students and thousands of alumni.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-38)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Reflection_Pond_%2815736953153%29.jpg/250px-Reflection_Pond_%2815736953153%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Reflection_Pond_(15736953153).jpg)

Reflecting Pond and Millican Hall

Main Campus is one of the safest branches nationally in comparison of all branches in the US. The percent of crimes in Main Campus decreased from 0.12% (in 2010) to 0.07% (in 2014) crimes per year.[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_][[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-39)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Rosen_%2815318251024%29.jpg/250px-Rosen_%2815318251024%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rosen_(15318251024).jpg)

#### Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona")]

Main article: [Lake Nona Medical City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Nona_Medical_City "Lake Nona Medical City")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/UcfComLakeNonaJune2010.jpg/250px-UcfComLakeNonaJune2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UcfComLakeNonaJune2010.jpg)

UCF College of Medicine at Lake Nona

The 50-acre (20-hectare) UCF Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona includes the [UCF College of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_College_of_Medicine "University of Central Florida College of Medicine") and the Burnett Biomedical Sciences Building. The [Burnham Institute for Medical Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnham_Institute_for_Medical_Research "Burnham Institute for Medical Research"), a [Veterans Affairs Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VA_hospital "VA hospital"), [Nemours Children's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemours_Children's_Hospital,_Florida "Nemours Children's Hospital, Florida"), [M.D. Anderson Cancer Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.D._Anderson_Cancer_Research_Institute "M.D. Anderson Cancer Research Institute"), turning the area into a medical city.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-Health_Sciences_Campus-43)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-mednews-45) The campus will also serve as the future home of the [UCF College of Nursing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCF_College_of_Nursing "UCF College of Nursing") and the newly approved [UCF College of Dental Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCF_College_of_Dental_Medicine "UCF College of Dental Medicine").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-46)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-47) The College of Medicine welcomed its charter class in August 2009.

Upon completion of construction, the campus could accommodate as many as 5,000 upper division, professional, and graduate students and faculty members in the health-related programs, and include up to two million square feet of research and instruction space.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-mednews-45)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-48)

## Administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Administration")]

See also: [List of presidents of the University of Central Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_University_of_Central_Florida "List of presidents of the University of Central Florida") and [List of University of Central Florida faculty and administrators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_University_of_Central_Florida_faculty_and_administrators "List of University of Central Florida faculty and administrators")

As a part of the [State University System of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_University_System_of_Florida "State University System of Florida"), UCF falls under the purview of the [Florida Board of Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Board_of_Governors "Florida Board of Governors"). The University of Central Florida is headed by the board of trustees, which governs the university, consisting of 13 appointed to staggered five-year terms by the Florida Board of Governors.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The [Student Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_Student_Government "University of Central Florida Student Government") president and the faculty chair also serve on the board for the duration of their one-year terms of office.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-pres-49)

The president of the University of Central Florida is the university's principal executive officer. The office was formed upon the university's creation in 1963. The president is appointed by the board of trustees with the consent of the Florida Board of Governors and leads the university through its daily business.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-50) Today, the president's office is in Millican Hall on the university's main campus, and the president lives in the Burnett House, also on the main campus.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The fourth president of UCF, [John C. Hitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hitt "John Hitt"), served from 1992 to 2018[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-51) and was succeeded by incumbent university president Dale Whittaker. After Whittaker resigned in 2019, Thad Seymour Jr. was appointed from his previous position as UCF's vice president for partnerships and chief innovation officer to serve as the university's interim president until the board of trustees chould choose a replacement.

Due to cutbacks in federal, state and local budgets, UCF has had over $140 million in funds cut from its operating budget since 2008.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-52) This included a $53 million cut to UCF's 2012–13 [fiscal year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_year "Fiscal year") budget by the Florida legislature.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-53)[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_] So far UCF has endured the budget cuts by implementing a hiring freeze, ending some faculty perks, such as free seminars, cutting executive pay, and wise management of funds.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-54) To help counter the budget decreases, the university received $18 million in funds from the [American Recovery and Reinvestment Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Recovery_and_Reinvestment_Act "American Recovery and Reinvestment Act").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-55) UCF's operating budget for the 2014–15 fiscal year is $1.5 billion, a 13.9% increase from the previous year.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf-6)[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_] UCF's [financial endowment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_endowment "Financial endowment"), administered by the University of Central Florida Foundation, Inc., was valued at $162 million in 2020.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf1819-56)

UCF's admission rate for first-time-in-college freshmen has declined from 61% of prospective students admitted in the fall of 2005, to 42% for fall 2020.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-:0-63)

34% of accepted applicants were in the top ten percent of their graduating class, while 72% of accepted applicants were in the top quarter of their high school [class rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_rank "Class rank").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-64) Freshmen enrolled in fall 2020 posted average [SAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAT "SAT") scores of 1320, [ACT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACT_(examination) "ACT (examination)") scores of 28.7 and average high school [weighted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_grading_in_the_United_States#Weighted_GPA "Academic grading in the United States") GPAs of 4.18.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-65) UCF is in the top 20 percent of universities in the nation for SAT average and the top 25 percent for GPA average.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-UCFEarnsaTop5-66) 71% of undergraduates receive financial aid. 90% of students receive scholarships through the [Florida Bright Futures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Bright_Futures "Florida Bright Futures") program.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-fin_aid-67) Forty percent of incoming freshman received [Advanced Placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Placement "Advanced Placement"), [International Baccalaureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Baccalaureate "International Baccalaureate"), or an equivalent college credit upon entrance, while 30% of the freshman class received merit based scholarships.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-fin_aid-67) The retention rate of the 2010 freshman class was 87%.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-commondataset-68)

More freshmen and transfer students applied to UCF during 2015 than any other public university in Florida, and UCF also awarded more bachelor's degrees than any other Florida public university that year.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-69)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-70) In 2010, UCF was ranked 2nd in Florida, and 34th in the United States, by the number of [National Merit Scholars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSAT/NMSQT "PSAT/NMSQT") enrolled.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-71)[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_] 335 National Merit Scholars enrolled at UCF for the fall 2020 term.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Classification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Classification")]

The University of Central Florida is [accredited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education_accreditation_in_the_United_States "Higher education accreditation in the United States") by the [Higher Learning Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_Learning_Commission "Higher Learning Commission") (HLC), a U.S. Department of Education–recognized institutional accreditor based in Chicago that historically served colleges in the [Midwestern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-ucfhlc-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-73) From 1970 to 2026, UCF was accredited by the [Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Association_of_Colleges_and_Schools "Southern Association of Colleges and Schools") (SACSCOC).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-ucfhlc-72) In 2022, Florida law (SB 7044; §1008.47) required public universities to change accreditors after each cycle; UCF received initial HLC accreditation in 2025, the first [State University System of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_University_System_of_Florida "State University System of Florida") institution to complete the switch.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-75)

Its academic calendar is based on the [semester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_term#Collegiate_calendars "Academic term") system,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-76) with the typical fall semester running from the end of August until the beginning of December and the typical spring semester running from the beginning of January through the beginning of May. In addition, UCF offers four different summer semesters, ranging from 6 to 12 weeks long.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-77) The university is [classified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Classification_of_Institutions_of_Higher_Education "Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education") as a "large four-year, primarily nonresidential" university with a "comprehensive doctoral" graduate instructional program and "highest research activity".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-Carnegie-78)

In the 2025 _U.S. News & World Report_ rankings, UCF was tied for 117th in the National Universities category (tied for 57th among "Top Public Schools") and tied for the 15th "most innovative school".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-Rankings_USNWR_NU-80) In addition, _U.S. News & World Report_ ranked the University of Central Florida as the 9th best in online bachelor's program in the nation in 2025.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-89)_[Aviation Week Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation\_Week\_Network "Aviation Week Network")_ also ranked UCF as the No. 1 provider of graduates to the U.S. aerospace and defense industry.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-90)_U.S. News & World Report_ ranked UCF No. 1 in the nation for "homeland/national security and emergency management" programs in 2026, for the third consecutive year.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-91)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-92)_[Shanghai Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai\_Ranking "Shanghai Ranking")_ Global Ranking of Academic Subjects, UCF ranked No. 1 in the U.S. for "transportation science and technology".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-93)

#### The Burnett Honors College

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: The Burnett Honors College")]

Main article: [The Burnett Honors College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Burnett_Honors_College "The Burnett Honors College")

The University Honors Program, administered by the Burnett Honors College is designed for 500 accomplished incoming undergraduates annually.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Undergraduates enrolled in the Honors College participate in smaller classes with faculty, including individual research programs or assigned research in the area of a sponsoring faculty member.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Another program offered by the college is Honors in the Major, which allows juniors and seniors to conduct original research within their major and write an undergraduate honors thesis.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-98)

#### College of Medicine

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: College of Medicine")]

Main article: [University of Central Florida College of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_College_of_Medicine "University of Central Florida College of Medicine")

The UCF College of Medicine was established in 2006 by the Florida Legislature and the Florida Board of Governors to increase opportunities for medical [education in Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_Florida "Education in Florida"). The College of Medicine welcomed its charter class of 41 students on August 3, 2009, and eventually will produce about 120 medical graduates a year.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-99)

With more than 4,300 applications for 41 available positions, UCF broke the state university record for most applications, and for 2009 it was the most selective medical school in the country.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-100)[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_] For the class of 2014, there were 3,761 applicants and only 60 were accepted.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-medstats-101)[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_] This initial class had the highest average MCAT score, 32.2, and GPA, 3.8, of any incoming class of medical students in the state.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-102) The inaugural class had a median age of 28, with 25% of the class composed of out-of-state students.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-medstats-101) The charter class completed their first year of courses on the UCF main campus, while the Lake Nona Medical City was completed.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Every member of the inaugural class received a full scholarship, including tuition and basic living expenses, for their entire four years at the university, valued at over $160,000.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-103)

The university aims for the college to become a research-intensive medical school, with the aid of [the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Burnett_School_of_Biomedical_Sciences "The Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences"), the [UCF Lake Nona Cancer Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCF_Lake_Nona_Cancer_Center?action=edit&redlink=1 "UCF Lake Nona Cancer Center (page does not exist)"), a [Veterans Affairs Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VA_hospital "VA hospital"), [Nemours Children's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemours_Foundation "Nemours Foundation"), [Tavistock Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tavistock_Group "Tavistock Group"), and a [M.D. Anderson Cancer Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.D._Anderson_Cancer_Research_Institute "M.D. Anderson Cancer Research Institute"), all located on the College of Medicine's Lake Nona campus.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-Health_Sciences_Campus-43)

### Limited access programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Limited access programs")]

Among the colleges, a number of undergraduate academic programs are termed "limited access programs" which are programs where student demand exceeds available resources thus making admission to such program competitive.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-107) Examples include academic programs taught under the Nicholson School of Communication and the music, theatre, dance, and medical laboratory sciences schools or departments.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-108)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-109)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-110)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-111) Students must apply to join these programs separately from admission to the university. Criteria for admission varies but is generally very selective and includes factors such as indicators of ability, performance, creativity, and talent. Arts programs require competitive auditions and have some of the smallest numbers of undergraduate majors in the university.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-catalog-94)

### Libraries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Libraries")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/UCFlibrary.jpg/250px-UCFlibrary.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCFlibrary.jpg)

John C. Hitt Library

Main article: [University of Central Florida Libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_Libraries "University of Central Florida Libraries")

UCF Libraries collections include over 2.2 million print volumes, 3.2 million microforms, 330,000 government documents, 10,000 full text electronic journal subscriptions, 660,000 e-books, 40,000 media titles, a base of 43,000 serial subscriptions, in addition to special collections and university archives materials.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf-6) Notable collections within the library include the Bryant West Indies collection, the Van Sickle Leftist Pamphlet collection, the Book Arts Collection, collections of materials on tourism and hospitality, and materials on the history of Central Florida.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] UCF Libraries is a partner within the [State University System of Florida Libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_University_System_of_Florida_Libraries "State University System of Florida Libraries").

Most of the print and media collection is housed in the John C. Hitt Library, which is located on UCF's main campus and is open to students, faculty and the public seven days a week. The library is five stories tall, and was the first academic building on campus.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-112)[Leonardo Nierman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Nierman "Leonardo Nierman")'s sculpture _Flame of Hope_ is displayed outside the entrance to the building, and Nierman's stained glass _Genesis_ window is exhibited on the third floor of the library building.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-113) In 2012, the main campus library was dedicated to honor John C. Hitt, UCF's fourth president, who at the time was celebrating his twentieth anniversary as university president.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-114) In addition to the John C. Hitt Library, Rosen College library, Downtown Library, Curriculum Materials Center, and the [Harriet F. Ginsburg Health Sciences Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_College_of_Medicine#Harriet_F._Ginsburg_Health_Sciences_Library "University of Central Florida College of Medicine"), UCF operates libraries at nine of its regional campuses throughout Central Florida.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-115)

The student newspaper, the _[Central Florida Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central\_Florida\_Future "Central Florida Future")_, at one time was housed on the upper floor of the library before moving to the [Central Florida Research Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Florida_Research_Park "Central Florida Research Park"). In 1984, a complete renovation of the original library was undertaken, as well as an addition that more than doubled the size of the building.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-116) University president [Trevor Colbourn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_University_of_Central_Florida_faculty_and_administrators "List of University of Central Florida faculty and administrators") dedicated the newly remodeled and expanded library in February 1985. A $64.4 million expansion of the Hitt Library, which would add 212,400 square feet (19,730 m 2) of space, as well as an Automated Retrieval System was recently[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] approved by the university's board of trustees but may be delayed due to budget cuts.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-117)

In 2022, the library began working on its 21st Century Library Project, a multi-phased plan designed to create additional space for student learning, technology, collaboration, and research expansion.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-118) The project upon completion will include the construction of a four-story automated retrieval center, increased quiet study space, and the creation of additional research and writing facilities on the fifth floor.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-119)

## Research

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Research")]

Further information: [University of Central Florida research centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_research_centers "University of Central Florida research centers")

The University of Central Florida fosters research among its thirteen academic colleges and schools, partnerships with corporations such as [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin"), [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney"), [Boeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing "Boeing"), [L3Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L3Harris "L3Harris"), [Siemens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens "Siemens"), [SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX"), and [Universal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Destinations_&_Experiences "Universal Destinations & Experiences").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-120)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-121)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-122)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-123)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-124) UCF also houses a satellite campus in Cocoa, FL, near [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center"). UCF is also a member of the [Florida High Tech Corridor Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_High_Tech_Corridor_Council "Florida High Tech Corridor Council").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-125) The university has made noted research contributions to aerospace, optics, modeling and simulation, digital media, engineering and computer science, business administration, education, and hospitality management.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-126)

UCF is [classified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Classification_of_Institutions_of_Higher_Education "Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education") among "[R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_research_universities_in_the_United_States "List of research universities in the United States")".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-Carnegie-78) According to the [National Science Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation "National Science Foundation"), UCF spent $215.3 million on research and development in 2018, ranking it 107th in the nation.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-127) In 2009, UCF directly influenced 26,000 jobs and $1.96 billion in economic activity. When UCF's economic impact is combined with that of the Central Florida Research Park, the university and park influenced 46,000 jobs and $3.84 billion in economic activity in 2009. The new [College of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_College_of_Medicine "University of Central Florida College of Medicine"), which opened in August 2009, will create an estimated 30,000 local jobs and have an economic impact of $7.6 billion in its first few years.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-128)[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_]

Metropolitan Orlando sustains the world's largest recognized cluster of modeling, simulation and training companies.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-seventhpark-37) Located directly south of the main campus is the [Central Florida Research Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Florida_Research_Park "Central Florida Research Park"), which is one of the largest research parks in the nation, providing more than 10,000 jobs.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Research Park is the 7th largest research park in the nation, with 2,700 [Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense"), [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") personnel, and direct support contractors.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Collectively, those defense organizations manage $5.2 billion in contracts every year.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-129) Many of the employees in Research Park work with UCF researchers and students on projects in the sciences, engineering, photonics and optics, modeling and simulation, and health-related fields.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The university also conducts research through numerous [institutions and centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_research_centers "University of Central Florida research centers"), including the [Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Research_and_Education_in_Optics_and_Lasers "Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers"), [Florida Solar Energy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Solar_Energy_Center "Florida Solar Energy Center"), [Institute for Simulation and Training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Simulation_and_Training "Institute for Simulation and Training") and [Institute for Economic Competitiveness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Economic_Competitiveness "Institute for Economic Competitiveness").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Space Institute

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Space Institute")]

UCF founded and governs the [Florida Space Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Space_Institute "Florida Space Institute") along with government partnerships such as NASA.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] As a result of their contributions, 17 UCF researchers had asteroids named after them.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] UCF researchers found and named a planet in 2012 after the discovery of UCF-1.01.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The [U.S. National Astronomy and Ionosphere Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arecibo_Observatory "Arecibo Observatory") is also managed by UCF.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-130) A 2015 _[Aviation Week & Space Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviation\_Week\_&\_Space\_Technology "Aviation Week & Space Technology")_ workforce study named UCF the No. 1 supplier of engineers to aerospace and defense industries.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-131)[_[outdated statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Cleanup "Wikipedia:Cleanup")_]

UCF's student body consists of 61,456 undergraduates and 10,002 graduate and professional students and 490 M.D. students from all [67 Florida counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Florida "List of counties in Florida"), all 50 states and 157 countries.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Study abroad programs allow UCF students to study and conduct research in 42 programs in 21 countries. The ten largest undergraduate disciplines at UCF are business management and administration, health professions and related, psychology, education, engineering, biology, multi/interdisciplinary studies, computer and information sciences, hospitality, and social sciences.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf-6)

UCF's enrollment has increased by over 60% this century, from 33,453 in 2000[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-2000_facts-135) to 64,318 in 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-facts_about_ucf-6) Of the more than 60,000 students, 11% are graduate and professional students, while women make up 55% of the student body. Nearly 20 percent of UCF faculty are minorities.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Due to budget decreases and increased demands on the university, the UCF board of trustees, with the approval of the board of governors and the Florida legislature, approved a 15% increase in tuition for the 2012–13 academic year.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-136) For the 2020–21 academic year, undergraduate tuition costs were [$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US$ "US$")212.28 per credit hour for in-state students and $748.89 per credit hour for out-of-state students.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-tuitionfees-137)[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] Graduate tuition costs were $369.65 per credit hour for in-state students and $1,194.05 per credit hour for out-of-state students.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-tuitionfees-137) Tuition for the medical school is $25,490 for both in-state and out-of-state students.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-tuitionfees-137) Estimated annual cost for undergraduate students is $22,2849 for Florida residents and $38,949 for non-Florida residents. Expected costs for graduate students are $22,072 for in-state students and $38,878 for out-of-state students.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-school_costs-138) About 8% of tuition fees are allocated to support the university's athletic programs.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-139)

UCF has over 400 registered student organizations,[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-kort-140)[intramural sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intramural_sports "Intramural sports"), and an active Student Government. The university encourages student activism through organizations such as the Office of Student Involvement, the Multicultural Student Center, the Campus Activities Board, and Volunteer UCF.

### Traditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Traditions")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Spirit_Splash.jpg/250px-Spirit_Splash.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Spirit_Splash.jpg)

Students in the Reflecting Pond during Spirit Splash

Spirit Splash is a [homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homecoming "Homecoming") tradition at UCF, and is traditionally the only time during the year that students are allowed into the Reflecting Pond. It has been named the best college tradition in Florida by _Florida Leader_ magazine,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-141) and among "The 20 Best College Traditions" by _[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business\_Insider "Business Insider")_.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-142)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-143)

Spirit Splash occurs the Friday before the Homecoming game, and serves as a pep rally where students descend into the pond to demonstrate school spirit. Spirit Splash began in 1995 when then-[Student Body President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_Student_Government "University of Central Florida Student Government") Miguel Torregrossa was pushed into the Reflecting Pond by one of his cabinet members and fellow students followed suit.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-144) Along with the thousands of students who attend, there are members of the community, local dignitaries, alumni, children and even dogs who come to join in on the festivities.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][Knightro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knightro "Knightro"), the [Marching Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_Knights "Marching Knights"), cheerleaders, [student athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCF_Knights "UCF Knights"), and dancers all participate in the pep rally, usually followed by a concert. Spirit Splash was made possible in part by weight testing performed on the Reflecting Pond in preparation for President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon")'s visit to the university to speak at its 1973 commencement. It was determined that the best way to protect the president would be to hold commencement in the pond itself, after being drained, so that [Secret Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secret_Service "United States Secret Service") agents could be stationed on the roofs of the adjacent buildings.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-145)

As is the case with many universities, UCF has superstitions regarding its seal. From their first day on campus for orientation, new students are told to never walk on the Pegasus seal in the center of the main floor of the Student Union.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] As the tradition is told, those who step on the seal will never graduate from UCF. Usually the seal is roped off with heavy black velvet ropes, but when the ropes are not in place, students can be seen carefully avoiding the seal. In 2005, Florida Leader magazine named this tradition the best college [superstition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstition "Superstition") in Florida.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-146)

### Housing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Housing")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/UCFPlazaTowers.JPG/250px-UCFPlazaTowers.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCFPlazaTowers.JPG)

 Towers at [Knights Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_Plaza "Knights Plaza")

The university currently houses over 12,000 on-campus students in eight different communities.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-147)[Residence hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residence_hall "Residence hall") style suites are available in the Libra, Apollo, Hercules, Nike, and Neptune communities. All of the residence hall suites have bathrooms shared between 2 or 3 rooms as opposed to communal bathrooms.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Apartment-style housing is available in the Academic Village (Nike and Hercules) communities, the Towers at [Knights Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_Plaza "Knights Plaza"), the Lake Claire Courtyard Apartments Community, and NorthView. UCF also has 400 beds at the Rosen College Apartments Community, located on the [Rosen College of Hospitality Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosen_College_of_Hospitality_Management "Rosen College of Hospitality Management") campus.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The majority of all on campus housing is occupied by freshman, though The Towers at Knights Plaza house mainly upper-classmen, student athletes, and honors students.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-Special_Interest_Communities-148)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_][[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-149)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-150) Residents of the Towers Communities and Rosen College Apartments sign annual contracts to rent their apartments for a full academic year (fall, spring, and summer), whereas residents of all other standard housing communities on the main campus sign academic contracts to rent their rooms only for one or two semesters at a time.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-151) Housing on the main campus typically fills to capacity well before the start of the fall semester, and cannot accommodate everyone who applies.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In addition, about 3,750 beds are available at the university-affiliated housing communities of Knights Circle and The Pointe at Central, which are off-campus apartment communities owned by The University of Central Florida Foundation, Inc.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-152)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-housing-153) and managed by Asset Living.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-154) These communities contain many UCF services such as Resident Assistants, [UCF Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida_Police_Department "University of Central Florida Police Department") service, reduced rent and offer shuttle service to and from campus on class days.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-155) The university also administers NorthView, which is owned and operated by UCF and located directly north of the main campus in [Oviedo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oviedo,_Florida "Oviedo, Florida"). NorthView houses 600 students, and includes a [Hillel Jewish Student Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillel:_The_Foundation_for_Jewish_Campus_Life "Hillel: The Foundation for Jewish Campus Life"), a Catholic Student Center, and a common space for other faith based organizations to use.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-156)

Greek housing is also available on the main campus in the Greek Park community, which consists of close to 500 beds. There are ten sororities and three fraternities housed on campus, with eleven fraternities offering housing off campus.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-housing-153)

### LEAD Scholars Academy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: LEAD Scholars Academy")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/UCF_LEAD_Scholars_Academy_Photo.jpg/250px-UCF_LEAD_Scholars_Academy_Photo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UCF_LEAD_Scholars_Academy_Photo.jpg)

LEAD Lounge

Founded in 1995 and eliminated on August 3, 2026, the LEAD Scholars Academy was a selective, two-year undergraduate leadership program at the University of Central Florida that combined academic coursework, experiential learning, and service projects.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-157) In the first year students completed LDR 2001 (Foundations of Leadership) and LDR 2002 (Leadership in Action); in the second year they enrolled in LDR 3950 (LEAD Seminar) and LDR 4105 (Leadership Capstone).[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-158)

Applicants typically participated in signature events such as a two-day REEL Retreat, annual Leadership Week panels and workshops.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-159) Graduates had the option to continue their leadership studies to receive a Leadership Studies minor or certificate [[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-160) and contributed collectively thousands of community service hours each year through partnerships with local nonprofits and campus organizations.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-161)

In 2019, the LEAD Scholars Academy was named “Outstanding Leadership Program of the Year” by the NASPA Student Leadership Programs Knowledge Community;[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-162) in 2023, it received the “Outstanding Program Bridging Civic Learning and Leadership Development” award from the NASPA Civic Learning & Democratic Engagement Knowledge Community;[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-163) and in 2023–24 the program earned a NASPA Excellence Bronze Award in the Leadership, Student Activities, & Related Areas category, recognizing its innovative student development initiatives.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-164)

The LEAD Scholars Academy was cited as a model leadership pipeline by Inside Higher Ed,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-165) noted by Georgetown’s The Feed for its role in improving Latine student retention through targeted support programs,[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-166) and featured on the NASPA SA Voices podcast in an interview with Stacey Malaret discussing the program’s impact and methodology.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-167)

### Recreation and fitness

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Recreation and fitness")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Front_view_of_Recreation_Center.jpg/250px-Front_view_of_Recreation_Center.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Front_view_of_Recreation_Center.jpg)

Recreation and Wellness Center

Many different recreational organizations and facilities are available on the UCF campus. Lake Claire is an on-campus lake with canoes, kayaks, and pedal boats available for rent (free to UCF students), and a small beachfront.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-168)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-169) In addition, UCF's [Challenge Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Challenge_Course "Challenge Course") is one of only five in the country to contain a high elements course.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-170)

UCF's main campus boasts the Recreation and Wellness Center and is located on the south side of campus, adjacent to the Academic Village. The center is open to all students, and paid memberships are available for non-students.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-171) The Wellness Center offer programs to boost students' understanding of their health, provides discounted blood and [STD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexually_transmitted_disease "Sexually transmitted disease") testing, staffs certified personal trainers, and teaches methods to maintain good health.

The UCF Recreation and Wellness Center, which opened in 2002, is a 150,000 square feet (14,000 m 2) building that comprises five programs: Intramural Sports, Sport Clubs, Outdoor Adventure, Fitness, and Aquatics.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-172) The main recreation center includes a custom [climbing wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climbing_wall "Climbing wall") with more than 20 different routes, as well as, tennis courts, sand volleyball courts, a disc golf course, numerous intramural sports fields, a leisure pool, and an outdoor lap pool.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-173)

The University of Central Florida's Student Government (UCF SG) is an advocacy group for the students who attend the university, representing the university's approximately 70,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. It is the largest student government within the state of Florida and one of the largest in the United States.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-174) UCF SG operates within a multimillion-dollar budget[_[quantify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_].[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-175) It funds and operates five campus departments—the Recreation and Wellness Center, the Office of Student Involvement, Student Legal Services, the A&SF Business Office, and the Student Union—while also providing around $1 million in funding to nearly 600 registered student organizations.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-asf-176)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-177)

### Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Central_Florida&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Media")]

KnightNews.com is the only digital student newspaper serving the UCF community, and it operates without oversight from the university administration.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-180) KnightNews.com won the College Press Freedom Award in 2016 for its work fighting for open government.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] A print newspaper, the _[Central Florida Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central\_Florida\_Future "Central Florida Future")_, was shut down in August 2016. The _Future,_ which also ran without university oversight, was one of the largest [student-run newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_newspaper "Student newspaper") in the United States.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] It focused on campus and local news coverage, but also featured national and international stories. The university itself publishes two magazines, _[Centric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centric\_(magazine) "Centric (magazine)")_ and _[Pegasus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegasus\_(University\_of\_Central\_Florida\_magazine) "Pegasus (University of Central Florida magazine)")._ _Centric_ is the official student magazine of the university, and _Pegasus_ is the official university magazine.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The university has operated [WUCF-FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WUCF-FM "WUCF-FM"), a [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") station, since 1978. The station broadcasts [Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") that reaches Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Brevard, Lake and Volusia counties in central Florida. They broadcast an Internet program that is heard worldwide.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-181) In 2011, the university purchased [WUCF-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WUCF-TV "WUCF-TV"), which is Central Florida's only [Public Broadcasting Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service "Public Broadcasting Service") (PBS) television station.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] As the region's sole PBS affiliate, the station broadcasts to an estimated population of 4.6 million people in its aerial viewing area.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-182)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Central_Florida#cite_note-183)

One limited access program at UCF is the Jazz Studies program, which launched a professional recording label for the university, [Flying Horse Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_Horse_Records "Flying Horse Records").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The program's faculty group, [The Jazz Professors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Jazz_Professors "The Jazz Professors"), and their student group, [The Flying Horse Big Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Flying_Horse_Big_Band "The Flying Horse Big Band"), have both issued professional recordings since 2011 for the university label.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
